title: Single-port inflatable video-assisted mediastinoscopic transhiatal esophagectomy for esophageal cancer in a patient with left upper lobe destruction secondary to remote pulmonary tuberculosis: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Surgical resection is the cornerstone of curative treatment for resectable esophageal cancer. However, transthoracic esophagectomy (TTE) requires one-lung ventilation (OLV), which may be poorly tolerated by patients with severely impaired pulmonary function. Inflatable video-assisted mediastinoscopic transhiatal esophagectomy combined with laparoscopy (IVMTE), which avoids OLV, may offer an alternative surgical approach for these patients. Case presentation A 70-year-old man presented with a 1-month history of dysphagia. Endoscopic biopsy confirmed mid-thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). He had a history of pulmonary tuberculosis with radiographic evidence of left upper lobe destruction. Pulmonary function testing revealed severe restrictive ventilatory impairment with impaired diffusing capacity, rendering him unable to tolerate transthoracic surgery. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, he underwent single-port inflatable video-assisted mediastinoscopic transhiatal esophagectomy combined with laparoscopy (SP-IVMTE), with an uneventful intraoperative course and no oxygen desaturation. Histopathology revealed a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma invading the adventitia, with negative margins and no lymph node metastasis (pT3N0M0). The patient had an uneventful postoperative recovery and was discharged on postoperative day 14. The patient had an uneventful postoperative recovery. Follow-up CT scans through 24 months showed no evidence of recurrence or metastasis, and at the 29-month clinical follow-up, he remained asymptomatic with normal oral intake. Conclusions For patients with severely compromised pulmonary reserve who are unable to tolerate a transthoracic approach, IVMTE may provide a feasible individualized surgical option for curative treatment of esophageal cancer.

title: Sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis presenting as an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background : Amyand's hernia, defined as the presence of the vermiform appendix within an inguinal hernia sac, is uncommon. Acute appendicitis within an Amyand's hernia is rarer, and a sliding variant in which the caecum contributes to the hernia sac adds further operative complexity. We report a case of sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis presenting as an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia. Case presentation: A 56-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a one-day history of a painful, irreducible right inguinoscrotal swelling on a background of a three-year hernia. He was constipated but continued to pass flatus and had no fever or urinary symptoms. Examination showed a tender irreducible right inguinoscrotal hernia with a soft, non-tender abdomen and no peritonism. The white cell count was 19 × 10⁹/L and C-reactive protein was 142 mg/L. Plain abdominal radiography showed dilated small bowel loops. Computed tomography was difficult to arrange on an emergency basis. Although ultrasonography was available, it was not requested because the clinical diagnosis of an incarcerated inguinal hernia was sufficiently compelling to warrant operative management, and the anticipated findings were unlikely to alter the decision to proceed with surgery. At exploration, the caecum was found to form part of the wall of the hernia sac within the right hemiscrotum, with a grossly inflamed appendix and inflammatory fluid. There was no features of bowel ischaemia or gangrene. Appendicectomy and primary non-mesh tissue repair were performed. Histology confirmed acute appendicitis. The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and the patient was well at three-week follow-up. Conclusion: Sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis should be considered as a differential diagnosis in patients presenting with an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia and disproportionate inflammatory markers. Although the diagnosis is often established intraoperatively, awareness of this possibility may improve operative preparedness. Intraoperative assessment of appendiceal inflammation, contamination and the sliding caecal anatomy should guide appendiceal management and the choice of hernia repair. In this patient, appendicectomy with primary tissue repair was followed by an uncomplicated early recovery.

title: Salvage computed tomography-guided brachytherapy for patients with postoperative vaginal recurrence of endometrial cancer
abstract: Abstract Background This study retrospectively analyzed the treatment outcomes of computed tomography (CT)-guided brachytherapy (BT) for vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery. Methods Patients with vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery who underwent CT-guided BT between were retrospectively analyzed. The primary endpoint was local control (LC). Secondary endpoints included regional recurrence-free survival (RRFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and late toxicities. Results 50 patients were included. External beam radiotherapy (EBRT) with a median total dose of 50 Gy was administered to 30 patients. The median number of BT fractions was five for patients with superficial recurrence and three for those with visible recurrence, respectively. The median total dose delivered to the high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) (equivalent dose in 2 Gy fractions; EQD2) was 70.5 Gy. The median follow-up period was 44.8 months. The 3-year LC, RRFS, DMFS, DFS, and OS rates were 85.6%, 82.9%, 65.1%, 46.0%, and 87.1%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, HR-CTV D90 was a significant prognostic factor for LC (p = 0.009). The 3-year LC rate was significantly higher in patients with HR-CTV D90 ≥ 67.3 Gy than in those with < 67.3 Gy (100% vs. 64.2%). In the multivariate analysis, tumor visibility and postoperative risk classification were significant prognostic factors for DMFS (p < 0.011 and p = 0.033, respectively). Conclusions CT-guided BT provides favorable local control in patients with vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery. However, distant metastases remain a major site of failure. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Construction of a Retinopathy of Prematurity Onset Prediction Model Using the Random Forest Machine Learning Algorithm
abstract: Abstract Objective: This study aimed to refine and validate a previously developed Random Forest prediction model for the onset of Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP), which was based on a machine learning approach. Methods: A retrospective study was conducted on 150 neonatal cases who met the inclusion criteria and underwent ROP screening at the Department of Neonatology, Wuzhou Workers' Hospital, Guangxi, China, between January 2024 and September 2024.1.Data on ROP-related risk factors and concurrent fundus screening results were collected by reviewing the electronic medical records (inpatient and follow-up outpatient) of the enrolled neonates.2.The top 15 risk factors identified from five distinct machine learning models were analyzed to identify the common risk factors among them.3.The Random Forest prediction model was validated. Results: 1.Nine common risk factors were identified from the top 15 factors across the five machine learning models: oxygen therapy, oxygen concentration, gestational age, birth weight, anemia of prematurity, neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS), necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), in vitro fertilization embryo transfer, and antibiotic use.2.Validation of the Random Forest model using the dataset from Wuzhou Workers' Hospital showed good performance on the validation set: AUC: 0.892, accuracy: 77.9%, specificity: 99.3%, sensitivity: 62.9%, precision: 89.9%. Conclusion: The Random Forest model, constructed using machine learning methods and incorporating predictive features such as oxygen therapy, oxygen concentration, gestational age, birth weight, anemia of prematurity, NRDS, NEC, in vitro fertilization embryo transfer, and antibiotic use, demonstrates good predictive value for ROP. This model holds potential for application in clinical screening of high-risk populations for retinopathy of prematurity.

1.Nine common risk factors were identified from the top 15 factors across the five machine learning models: oxygen therapy, oxygen concentration, gestational age, birth weight, anemia of prematurity, neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS), necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), in vitro fertilization embryo transfer, and antibiotic use.2.Validation of the Random Forest model using the dataset from Wuzhou Workers' Hospital showed good performance on the validation set: AUC: 0.892, accuracy: 77.9%, specificity: 99.3%, sensitivity: 62.9%, precision: 89.9%.

Conclusion:

The Random Forest model, constructed using machine learning methods and incorporating predictive features such as oxygen therapy, oxygen concentration, gestational age, birth weight, anemia of prematurity, NRDS, NEC, in vitro fertilization embryo transfer, and antibiotic use, demonstrates good predictive value for ROP. This model holds potential for application in clinical screening of high-risk populations for retinopathy of prematurity.

title: Spatial Alignment of Parkinson’s Disease-Related Quantitative MRI Alterations with Dopaminergic Topography
abstract: Abstract Objective Parkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by a degeneration of dopaminergic neurons not only in the nigrostriatal pathways, but also in subcortical and cortical structures. Given the widespread dopaminergic innervation, PD dopamine-related dysfunction may contribute to microstructural alterations beyond the primary site of pathology. Multiparametric mapping (MPM) enables quantification of tissue biophysical properties informing the brain’s microstructure. We hypothesized that PD-related MPM alterations would show distinct spatial associations with pre- and postsynaptic dopaminergic markers. Methods 31 patients with PD and 68 healthy controls underwent a 3T MRI. We used unthresholded MPM t-maps derived from group-difference analysis to assess spatial correlation with PET-derived maps of the dopamine transporter (DAT), [ 18 F]-fluoro-L-DOPA (FDOPA), and dopamine D1 and D2 receptors. Results Proton density alterations negatively correlated with DAT (rho = 0.355, p spatial = 0.0010) and FDOPA (rho = 0.168, p FDR = 0.0080) across whole-brain gray matter. Subcortically, MPM-dopaminergic associations were structure-specific, showing concordant, same-direction associations between FDOPA and D1. Cortically, associations were more consistent, predominantly negative and driven by DAT and FDOPA. Within cortical ROIs, presupplementary and supplementary motor areas showed the most robust associations, driven by proton density (preSMA: rho = 0.428 to 0.760; SMA: rho = 0.284 to 0.789, all p FDR < 0.0001). Interpretation: PD-related microstructural-dopaminergic associations were structure- and modality-specific. Subcortically, FDOPA and D1 consistently tracked microstructural alterations, potentially reflecting coupled degeneration of dopaminergic synthesis capacity and postsynaptic receptor density. Cortically, DAT and FDOPA most robustly tracked proton density-related alterations, potentially indicating distinct and mainly neuroinflammation-driven microstructural processes beyond the primary nigrostriatal network.

title: Transthoracic echocardiography for initial screening of single coronary artery anomaly: a case with multimodal imaging evaluation
abstract: Abstract Single coronary artery anomaly (SCA) is a rare congenital coronary malformation with only one aortic coronary ostium supplying the whole myocardium. Clinical outcomes mainly depend on the anatomical course of the aberrant vessel. We report a 73-year-old female presenting with intermittent precordial chest pain. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a dilated right coronary artery (RCA) with normal ostial location, non-visualization of the left coronary artery ostium, and diastolic low-resistance arterial flow signal within the interventricular septum along the expected left anterior descending artery (LAD) territory. Coronary computed-tomography angiography (CCTA) demonstrated right-dominant coronary circulation, absence of the native left coronary artery, and an abnormally extended posterior descending artery travelling into the anterior interventricular groove. Multimodal imaging highly suggested Lipton-Yamanaka type R-I SCA. The patient received conservative medical therapy for co-existing mild coronary atherosclerosis. This case underlines TTE as a valuable first-line screening tool for congenital coronary anomalies. Nevertheless, definitive subtyping requires CCTA or invasive coronary angiography.

title: [18F]NaF PET Radiomics and Coronary Calcium Score Progression: Associations Beyond Baseline Calcium Score and TBR
abstract: Abstract Background: [ 18 F]NaF positron emission tomography (PET) can quantify coronary calcification activity before coronary calcium score (CCS) progression, which is a surrogate measure of cardiovascular disease risk. It remains uncertain whether advanced PET quantification, including radiomics, improves prediction of CCS progression. Participants with type 2 diabetes underwent baseline [ 18 F]NaF PET/CT, baseline CCS and a follow-up CCS after 2 years. CCS progression was evaluated on a per-patient and a per-artery level. [ 18 F]NaF activity was evaluated using the TBR max , and radiomics features. Logistic regression models were used to determine the features most associated with CCS progression. Results: In total, 91 participants (median age [interquartile range]: 66 [60 – 70], 71.4% male) were examined. In total, 68 patients (74.7%) demonstrated CCS progression. Clinical variables and baseline CCS discriminated CCS progressors and non-progressors modestly (AUC 0.72, 95% CI 0.55–0.86). The TBR max demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.73–0.92), while multi-feature radiomics models achieved the highest discrimination performance (AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.80–0.97). A total of 211 coronary arteries (58.0%) demonstrated CCS progression. The combined CCS and TBR max model discriminated CCS progressors and non-progressors modestly (AUC of 0.67, 95% CI 0.60–0.73), while the multi-feature radiomics demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.77, 95% CI: 0.70–0.84). Conclusions: [ 18 F]NaF PET radiomics improves prediction of CCS progression compared with baseline CCS, clinical features, and the TBR max .

title: Key performance indicators for organized risk stratified prostate cancer screening in Europe: first results from the PRAISE-U and EUCanScreen pilots and the Swedish organised prostate cancer testing programme
abstract: Abstract Background. Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer in men in the European Union. Following the 2022 Council Recommendation to evaluate organised screening based on prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), PRAISE-U defined 21 harmonised key performance indicators (KPIs). We report their first empirical values from the five PRAISE-U pilots and, through a common survey, from EUCanScreen pilots and the Swedish organised prostate cancer testing (OPT) programme. Methods. In PRAISE-U, men aged 50–69 years at five pilot sites in Spain, Lithuania, Poland and Ireland were invited to risk-stratified screening comprising PSA testing, first-level risk stratification, MRI for intermediate or high risk and selective biopsy, with prospective capture in a central REDCap database. EUCanScreen pilots and the Swedish organised prostate cancer testing (OPT) programme reported the same KPIs through an online survey. Results. Twelve programmes reported KPI values. Across the five PRAISE-U pilots, participation ranged from 7.1% to 43.0%, PSA exceeded 3 ng/ml in 9.2–15.0%, and compliance was 76.4–96.0% for first-level risk assessment, 89.9–98.3% for MRI and 78.9–99.0% for biopsy. Detection ranged from 8 to 26 per 1,000 screened in PRAISE-U and from 4.3 to 28 across all programmes. ISUP grade 1 accounted for 20.3–81.4% of cancers, active-surveillance uptake for 14.8–100%, and mean time from PSA result to MRI for 19–114 days; external values fell broadly within the PRAISE-U ranges. Thirteen of 21 KPIs were fully reported by all five pilots, all describing the diagnostic pathway; retention and the three impact indicators were reported only by Sweden, which reported 19 of 21. Conclusions. Diagnostic-pathway KPIs were measurable under pilot conditions, whereas programme-level indicators required a defined target population or registry linkage. Sweden, the only population-based programme, reported retention and long-term impact, identifying the infrastructure needed before organised PCa screening can be monitored at scale.

title: Versajet® Hydrosurgery for Primary Axillary Hyperhidrosis with Osmidrosis: First Vietnamese Case Report with Histopathology
abstract: Abstract Background Conventional minimally invasive surgical techniques for axillary hyperhidrosis (e.g., cannula-assisted suction-curettage) carry risks of subdermal vascular plexus injury and flap necrosis (10–15%) [1] . The Versajet® Hydrosurgery System, employing the Venturi effect with high-pressure saline jet and continuous suction without thermal injury, represents a potential alternative [2,3] . Case presentation : A 33-year-old Vietnamese male (BMI 33.3 kg/m²) presented with 16-year history of bilateral primary axillary hyperhidrosis with osmidrosis (onset at age 18), HDSS 3 bilaterally, wet earwax phenotype (suggesting ABCC11 G-allele), DLQI 9/30, Park-Shin grade 3, meeting 5/6 Hornberger criteria [4] . Methods Surgery was performed on 23 April 2026 under Klein tumescent anesthesia (lidocaine 480 mg + epinephrine 1:1,000,000 + 500 mL 0.9% NaCl; 100 mL/axilla infiltration). The Versajet® II with a 45°/14 mm handpiece at power 6–8 (574 bar/8,330 psi) was used, consuming 500 mL 0.9% NaCl and 15 minutes of debridement per axilla through a 5-cm incision parallel to the axillary crease. Outcomes were assessed at 1 and 3 months using HDSS, DLQI, Park-Shin, and VSS, with paired pre-/post-excision histopathology. Results Total operative time was 100 minutes with blood loss < 30 mL and no intraoperative complications. VAS pain was 3/10 on days 1–3, resolving to 0/10 by day 10. At 3 months: HDSS 3→1, DLQI 9→1, Park-Shin 3→1, VSS 4/14, Clavien-Dindo grade I, patient satisfaction 5/5. Histopathology demonstrated 68.8–75.0% apocrine gland reduction and 32.3–45.5% eccrine gland reduction with preserved hair follicle architecture. Conclusion Hydrosurgery with the Versajet® System demonstrated high technical feasibility, significant clinical efficacy, and objective histopathological evidence of selective apocrine gland reduction while preserving the subdermal vascular plexus. Larger prospective cohort studies with long-term follow-up are warranted to standardize parameters and assess recurrence.

title: Enhanced Breast Cancer Classification by Integrating CNN and ViT on the CBIS-DDSM Mammography Dataset
abstract: Abstract Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of mortality among women worldwide, necessitating early and accurate diagnostic methods to improve patient outcomes. This study presents a novel hybrid approach for breast cancer classification by integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures, specifically applied to the publicly available CBIS-DDSM mammography dataset. The initial phase employs a CNN model, which excels in localized feature extraction through convolutional layers, to identify key patterns related to benign and malignant tumors. However, CNNs inherently focus on local features and may overlook broader contextual relationships within the image. To overcome this limitation, the study introduces a hybrid framework that combines CNN with the Vision Transformer model. ViT utilizes self-attention mechanisms to capture long-range dependencies and global context, complementing the localized feature extraction capability of CNNs. By integrating these two deep learning paradigms, the hybrid model effectively captures both fine-grained local details and overarching structural patterns within mammograms. Experimental results indicate that synergy results in an improved classification accuracy. The enhanced performance of the combined CNN-ViT model underscores the potential of hybrid deep learning strategies in medical image analysis. Moreover, this approach demonstrates robust generalization on the CBIS-DDSM dataset, which includes diverse mammographic cases. The findings not only provide a pathway to more reliable breast cancer detection tools but also contribute to reducing diagnostic burden and improving early intervention strategies.

title: EndoVLA-OOV: Language-Conditioned Out-of-View Target Acquisition in Robotic Endoscopy
abstract: The scan-then-revisit workflow of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy requires bringing a previously observed suspicious region back into view for closer inspection. Acquiring such targets requires translating anatomical and appearance descriptions into camera motions from partial observations of a confined, deformable environment. We present EndoVLA-OOV, a language-conditioned vision-language-action policy for out-of-view target acquisition in robotic endoscopy. The policy adapts a pretrained backbone to continuous two-degree-of-freedom distal bending commands and combines initial, intermediate, and current images to guide search. To support policy learning, we provide an open-source VLA dataset containing 1,050 episodes across six tasks and approximately 262k observation-action pairs. Physical evaluation spans wet-lens and low-light conditions, two unseen stomach phantoms, and cross-embodiment transfer to an unseen ex-vivo environment. In the cross-embodiment evaluation, the full-data policy achieves 93.3% target acquisition success (28/30). In a controlled training-data comparison, expanding the corpus from 312 to 1,050 episodes increases acquisition success from 40.0% to 90.0% under the same model, training, and test configuration. Instruction and observation interventions further support the use of language and temporal context in the evaluated acquisition tasks. These results support language-guided endoscopic revisitation across the evaluated environments and robot embodiments and demonstrate the benefit of expanded task-specific demonstrations.

title: Arbitrary-Scale Anisotropic 3D MRI Super-Resolution with Gaussian Prototypes
abstract: Reducing MRI acquisition time improves patient comfort, reduces motion artefacts, and increases scanner throughput. Clinical protocols often shorten acquisitions by sacrificing spatial resolution, particularly along the slice axis. Super-resolution can recover higher-resolution images, but existing methods are typically specialised to one scale or acquisition geometry, limiting their use across heterogeneous clinical protocols. We present GSMR3D, a continuous volumetric model that reconstructs arbitrary isotropic and anisotropic resolutions with a single checkpoint per MRI contrast. It combines a learned dictionary of anisotropic 3D Gaussian prototypes with scale-conditioned frequency encoding and an exact measurement-consistency projection, keeping reconstructions consistent with the acquired low-resolution data. We train separate models on 3,731 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted and 30,254 T1-weighted brain MRI volumes from clinical and population-based cohorts. We evaluate GSMR3D against geometry-specific specialists for isotropic, in-plane, and through-plane super-resolution using reconstruction quality and downstream tasks: brain tumour segmentation, brain-metastasis detection, and brain parcellation. GSMR3D outperforms specialists at isotropic $2\times$ and achieves better LPIPS, DISTS, and FID across all geometries, although specialists retain higher PSNR in anisotropic settings. It more faithfully preserves glioma segmentations across all geometries, achieves the highest lesion sensitivity on an independent brain-metastasis cohort, and the highest brain-parcellation agreement for isotropic and in-plane reconstruction. Reconstruction takes about 6s per volume, adding little overhead relative to acquisition-time savings. GSMR3D offers a flexible approach to MRI scan-time reduction with one model per contrast across geometries while preserving information relevant to downstream tasks.

title: Multimodal modeling of the ictal onset zone in refractory insular epilepsy and seizure outcome of magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial therapy: A pediatric single-center retrospective study.
abstract: This study was undertaken to evaluate seizure outcomes after magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy (MRgLITT) in children with insular epilepsy and to assess how the extent of ablation overlaps with multimodal definitions of the ictal onset zone (IOZ). We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including consecutive pediatric patients treated with MRgLITT for insular epilepsy. All patients underwent presurgical evaluation including electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and stereo-EEG (SEEG) were performed in negative-MRI cases. Epileptic zone was identified by visual analysis of SEEG recording. Postablation contrast-enhancing volumes were manually segmented and coregistered with IOZ estimates derived from Multi-centre Epilepsy Lesion Detection (MELD) MRI analysis, FDG-PET voxel-based analysis, and the Epileptogenicity Index, when available. Spatial concordance between modalities was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients, and the proportion of each IOZ modality encompassed within the ablation volume was correlated with postoperative seizure outcomes (International League Against Epilepsy classification). Eight children (median age = 10.4 years, range = 2.3-17) were included, with a median postoperative follow-up of 38 months. Two patients had insular tumors, and both achieved seizure freedom after complete ablation. Among the six MRI-negative patients, FDG-PET revealed insular hypometabolism in four, MELD detected a median of one insular cluster (range 1-3), and SEEG identified focal insular ictal activity in three cases. Overall, four negative-MRI patients achieved seizure freedom: three after MRgLITT alone and one after MRgLITT combined with frontal opercular resection. One transient postoperative aphasia was observed. Intermodality spatial concordance was low across all comparisons. A greater proportion of FDG-PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes (p = .012). MRgLITT is an effective and safe treatment option for focal insular epilepsy in children, either as standalone therapy or in a combined approach. Optimal outcome depends on accurate preoperative delineation of the IOZ and its complete ablation.

Overall, four negative-MRI patients achieved seizure freedom: three after MRgLITT alone and one after MRgLITT combined with frontal opercular resection. One transient postoperative aphasia was observed. Intermodality spatial concordance was low across all comparisons. A greater proportion of FDG-PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes (p = .012). MRgLITT is an effective and safe treatment option for focal insular epilepsy in children, either as standalone therapy or in a combined approach. Optimal outcome depends on accurate preoperative delineation of the IOZ and its complete ablation.

title: Intratumoral and Peritumoral Functional Connectivity Reveals Network-Level Signatures of Glioma.
abstract: Gliomas are recognized as network-level diseases that remodel functional connectivity across the brain. Using resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data from 306 patients with pathologically confirmed glioma at two hospitals, we delineated individualized intra- and peritumoral functional networks to quantify tumor-related alterations. Two novel indices-the ratio of intratumoral functional regions (RIFR) and ratio of peritumoral tumor-related regions (RPTR)-were proposed to describe network remodeling. Both indices were related to pathological, structural, functional, cognitive, language, and survival measures. Lower RIFR indicated diminished intratumoral connectivity and worse prognosis, while higher values reflected preserved network integration and longer survival. Models incorporating network features yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90 in training and 0.86-0.88 in external validation. Supporting analyses suggested that intratumoral functional regions are associated with distinct molecular and cellular characteristics. These findings suggest that intra- and peritumoral networks reflect biologically and functionally distinct tumor subregions and are associated with network-level alterations, brain function, and patient outcome. Interpretation is limited by the hemodynamic basis of rs-fMRI, incomplete data, and limited intraoperative validation. These findings identify individualized intra- and peritumoral connectivity measures as candidate markers of glioma-associated network remodeling and prognosis that require prospective, multimodal validation.

title: Bilateral Breast Gradient Insert Prototype for Strong Diffusion Encoding at 3 T.
abstract: Diffusion MRI has shown promise for breast cancer screening, lesion characterization, and treatment response monitoring without contrast agents, but further translation is constrained by the gradient performance of conventional systems. The aim of this work is to develop a single-axis high-performance bilateral plug-and-play breast gradient insert to enable strong-gradient diffusion MRI. An in-house breast gradient insert and bed-tabletop was constructed entirely from commercially available materials, providing a cost-effective solution compatible with existing MRI systems. Its wiring pattern was optimized for torque and force balancing, power dissipation, and target field performance. Evaluation included gradient field characterization, peripheral nerve stimulation simulation verification, and temperature and eddy current assessment. The setup was used for imaging of a diffusion phantom based on soy lecithin across a range of b values. Gradient efficiency ranged from 0.61 to 2.8 mT/m/A, enabling diffusion MRI using local strengths up to 420 mT/m (150 A). No peripheral nerve stimulation was observed during tests on five healthy volunteers. Eddy currents were successfully characterized, revealing a linear first order component with an amplitude of 0.03% of the applied gradient field. Imaging experiments demonstrated the feasibility of acquiring b = 10 000 s/mm2 volumes with a TE of 78 ms, compared with 161 ms when using the scanner gradients (40 mT/m). This work demonstrates a dedicated bilateral breast gradient insert for safe and feasible strong-gradient breast diffusion MRI and represents a first step toward dedicated hardware for breast cancer detection and characterization without contrast agents.

title: Inertial Navigation Assisted Motion Correction for Brain MRI.
abstract: To assess the utility of inertial sensors for estimating parameters describing rigid body motion of the head, and to reduce motion related artifact through a hybrid prospective steering of the rotation via the sensor and retrospective realignment of translation via the MRI data. Inertial sensors are widely used for Earth navigation problems. However, drift accumulation from integrating noisy signals makes them impractical for MRI motion correction at millimeter resolution over minute-long scans. Prior work has shown that the MRI system's B0 and gravity are approximately orthogonal and can be exploited as reference vectors for 3-DOF orientation estimation. We introduce a hybrid inertial measurement-based method, which uses these fields to estimate 3-DOF orientation directly, without integration, thereby eliminating random walk. The remaining 3-DOF translation is recovered via phase correlation from the MRI data. We validate the efficacy of this hybrid method retrospectively using a 3D radial koosh-ball sequence and prospectively using 2D EPI time-series acquisition during volunteer motions. IMU-based orientation estimation followed by phase correlation achieved a mean accuracy of 0.6° and 0.4 pixels across all experiments. Image quality improved when motion correction was applied in all volunteer scans for both retrospective and prospective correction cases. The proposed method measured head motion in the MRI scanner with high accuracy at unprecedented sampling rates and enabled both retrospective and prospective correction, improving image quality by aligning k-space data and reducing motion artifacts.

title: Effect of ultrasound-guided visual biofeedback performed by midwives on duration of second stage of labor: randomized controlled trial.
abstract: To investigate whether coached maternal pushing using transperineal ultrasound (TPUS)-guided visual biofeedback, performed by midwives, reduces the duration of the second stage of labor and affects the mode of delivery in nulliparous women receiving epidural analgesia. This was a single-center randomized controlled trial of nulliparous women with a singleton term pregnancy with an estimated fetal weight of 2500-4000 g, who were in the active stage of labor and were receiving epidural analgesia, conducted between May 2021 and August 2024. Consenting participants were assigned randomly to one of two groups: the study group (sonographic-coaching group), who were coached using TPUS-guided visual biofeedback, or the control group (traditional-coaching group), who were coached using the traditional vaginal technique. Coached maternal pushing with TPUS-guided visual biofeedback included a demonstration of the direction of effective pushing by visualizing the real-time downward movement of the fetal head on a television screen in front of the woman. Coaching sessions were conducted following epidural administration during the active stage of labor and after the diagnosis of complete cervical dilatation, with an additional session conducted if delivery had not occurred within 2 h after complete cervical dilatation. Coaching was led exclusively by midwives, with no involvement of obstetricians. Outcomes were compared between the groups. A total of 327 women were randomized and included, comprising 168 women in the sonographic-coaching group and 159 in the traditional-coaching group. Demographic and baseline characteristics, including maternal body mass index and rates of labor induction and oxytocin use, were similar in both groups. The second stage of labor was significantly shorter in the sonographic-coaching group compared with the traditional-coaching group (mean ± SD, 107 ± 59 min vs 132 ± 71 min; P = 0.001). The sonographic-coaching group also showed lower rates of second-degree or higher perineal tears (65.4% vs 77.3%; P = 0.020) and intrapartum fever (8.9% vs 16.4%; P = 0.043). Other secondary outcomes, including neonatal birth weight and 5-min Apgar score, did not differ significantly between the groups. No significant differences were observed in the mode of delivery. Coached maternal pushing using TPUS-guided visual biofeedback, performed by midwives, significantly reduced the duration of the second stage of labor and the incidence of second-degree or higher perineal tears and intrapartum fever. Larger studies are warranted to further assess its impact on delivery outcome. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

title: A multi-stage multimodal learning model for functional outcomes prediction in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Predicting functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains challenging due to the complex and dynamic nature of disease progression. Existing methods typically rely on single-stage imaging or limited multimodal fusion, failing to fully capture disease progression and cross-modal complementarity. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates multi-stage imaging and clinical notes for 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) prediction. The proposed model leverages a shared foundation model with Low-Rank Adaptation to encode pre- and post-treatment images. It further introduces a shared feature extraction module and a stage-specific feature extraction module to disentangle shared and stage-specific representations, enabling effective modeling of disease progression across stages. In addition, a bidirectional cross-attention module is employed to enhance semantic alignment between imaging features and clinical notes. Experiments on multi-stage NCCT and MRI datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms single-modality baselines, achieving AUCs of 0.9147 and 0.9479, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of both the multi-stage interaction design and the multimodal fusion strategy. These results suggest that integrating pre- and post-treatment imaging with clinical notes can improve prognostic performance, providing a practical solution for individualized outcome prediction in AIS patients following EVT.

title: Photon counting detector CTA for prostate arterial evaluation during the workup for prostate artery embolization.
abstract: To evaluate small field of view (FOV) ultra-high spatial resolution pelvic photon-counting detector prostate CT angiograms (UHR PCD CTA) for identifying prostate arterial anatomy and extraprostatic anastomoses in patients undergoing workup for prostate artery embolization (PAE). IRB-approved retrospective imaging and electronic medical record review of men who consecutively underwent UHR PCD CTA for PAE workup at our institution from 8/1/2022 to 12/1/2024. UHR PCD CTAs were evaluated by two vascular and interventional radiologists for main and accessory candidate prostatic arteries (PA/s) and anastomoses to penile, bladder, or rectal arteries. A main PA was defined as supplying the central gland and an accessory PA was defined as supplying the peripheral zone. PAs were categorized using the Carnevale classification. In patients who proceeded to PAE, digital subtraction angiograms (DSA) were retrospectively compared with UHR PCD CTA findings. UHR PCD CTA was obtained prior to PAE consultation for 50 men. We evaluated 100 pelvic sides, identifying 180 candidate PAs with a median of 3 candidate PAs per patient (mean, 3.6; range, 2-7). Overall, 56% (101/180) of candidate PAs were main and 44% (79/180) were accessory. Abridged Carnevale classifications: Type 5-21% (38/180). Eight accessory candidate PAs arose from the superior rectal artery. At least one candidate anastomosis arose from 40% (72/180) of candidate PAs. Of 95 total candidate anastomoses, 69 were extraprostatic (30 rectal, 20 bladder, 19 penile) and 26 were intraprostatic collaterals; 56% (53/95) arose from accessory and 44% (42/95) from main candidate PAs. Twenty-eight of 50 (56%) men underwent PAE, during which 72% (74/103) of available candidate PAs were selected, and prostatic supply was confirmed by DSA in 100% (74/74) of selected vessels. Small FOV UHR PCD CTA is useful in identifying candidate PA supply, as well as potential extraprostatic anastomoses, providing an arterial roadmap for PAE planning. Candidate PA supply was confirmed by DSA in all selected vessels among patients who proceeded to PAE.

title: Structured MRI reporting for deep pelvic endometriosis: objective report quality and surgeon-perceived clinical utility in a randomized comparative study.
abstract: To compare structured and free-text MRI reporting in terms of objective report quality and surgeon ratings of perceived clinical utility in suspected deep pelvic endometriosis. In this single-center randomized reader study, 20 radiology residents were assigned to free-text or structured reporting. Five residents became unavailable before report generation and provided no outcome data. The remaining 15 readers completed the same 22 pelvic MRI examinations, generating 330 reports: 154 free-text and 176 structured reports. Reports were compared with an imaging reference standard established by two pelvic radiologists through independent review and consensus adjudication. The primary endpoint was clinically weighted completeness. Secondary endpoints included unweighted completeness, explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference, positive findings unsupported by the expert imaging reference, and reporting time. Objective outcomes were analyzed using mixed-effects models or Poisson generalized estimating equations. In an exploratory paired assessment, two expert gynecologic surgeons evaluated 44 reports, comprising one free-text and one structured report for each MRI examination. Structured reporting was associated with an 8.1%-point increase in completeness compared with free-text reporting (95% CI, 4.1-12.1; p < 0.001) and a 5.6%-point increase in clinically weighted completeness (95% CI, 1.3-10.0; p = 0.011). Reporting time was 4.52 min longer with structured reporting (95% CI, 3.05-5.99; p < 0.001). Structured reporting was also associated with more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference (rate ratio, 2.94; 95% CI, 1.73-4.98; p < 0.001). These discrepancies were mainly explicit compartment-based negative statements. In the exploratory surgeon assessment, structured reports received higher ratings for perceived completeness, usefulness for clinical decision-making, and adequacy to clinical needs, whereas clarity ratings were similar between formats. Structured MRI reporting was associated with higher objective completeness and, in an exploratory assessment, higher surgeon ratings for several dimensions of perceived clinical utility. These findings should be balanced against longer reporting time and more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference.

title: Divergent approaches to rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease: a comparative analysis of international clinical practice guidelines.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. We compared international and regional clinical practice guidelines to identify agreement, differences, and gaps in RA-ILD care. We conducted a narrative comparative review of five guideline groups: ERS/EULAR, ACR/CHEST, EULAR, PANLAR, and ALAT. Recommendations were assessed across screening, diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment, together with their methodological approaches. Diagnostic recommendations showed the greatest agreement: ILD-focused guidelines emphasized high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), pulmonary function tests, and multidisciplinary evaluation. Screening recommendations differed: ERS/EULAR and ACR/CHEST favored risk-based assessment, whereas ALAT proposed a broader approach that included lung ultrasound as an adjunct, without replacing HRCT. For established RA-ILD, ACR/CHEST suggested, as implementation guidance, pulmonary function testing every 3-12 months during the first year and HRCT when clinically indicated; ERS/EULAR proposed pulmonary function testing every 3-6 months in the first years and periodic HRCT. Treatment showed the greatest divergence. ACR/CHEST conditionally recommended mycophenolate, rituximab, azathioprine, and cyclophosphamide as first-line ILD therapies, whereas ALAT emphasized integrated control of articular and pulmonary disease, particularly with abatacept or rituximab. EULAR and PANLAR primarily addressed RA treatment and did not provide dedicated RA-ILD algorithms. Antifibrotic treatment was considered mainly in progressive fibrosing disease. Guidelines converge on HRCT-based evaluation but differ in screening, monitoring intervals, and treatment priorities. These differences reflect their scope, methodology, and limited RA-ILD-specific evidence. Prospective comparative studies are needed to inform more consistent care.

title: Combined use of orbital soft tissue volume and retinal microvessel density for diagnosing dysthyroid optic neuropathy.
abstract: To (i) detect changes in orbital soft tissue and retinal microstructure occurring in thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO), (ii) investigate the relationship between these variables and their bearing on visual impairment, and (iii) determine their combined diagnostic utility for dysthyroid optic neuropathy (DON). Enrolled in this retrospective study were patients with TAO eyes, which included the DON group, equivocal DON (eDON) and non-DON (nDON). Patients were divided into three experimental groups: DON (n = 18 eyes), eDON (n = 24 eyes), and nDON (n = 20 eyes). At the same time, a healthy control (C) group was included (n = 30 eyes). A three-dimensional (3D) volume index, obtained by reconstructing orbital soft tissue via computed tomography (CT) and Mimics software, was used. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A) was used to monitor and record retinal microstructural properties, i.e., microvessel density and thickness. The DON group had significantly lower density and thickness of the retinal vasculature compared to the other groups (p < 0.05), with the exception of deep macular capillary density (MDRCP-VD), which was not statistically significant. In terms of soft-tissue volumes, the DON group had considerably higher orbital fat (OFV/BOV) and extraocular muscle indices (EOMV/BOV) than did the other groups; in contrast, the muscle cone inner volume index (MCIV/BOV) was lower (p < 0.05). A combination of the macular superficial retinal capillary plexuses (MSCRP-VD), optic nerve head vessel density-whole images (ONH-wiVD), MCIV/BOV, and EOMV/BOV yielded the highest values (AUC: 0.954, sensitivity: 95%, specificity: 88.1%) for the diagnosis of DON compared to the other groups. EOMV/BOV plus MCIV/BOV, combined with MSRPC-VD plus ONH-wiVD, appears to provide the most accurate diagnostic guideline for DON. Further, 3D reconstructions of orbital soft tissue, in conjunction with OCT-A images, offer an innovative approach not only for preventing permanent loss of vision but also for enhancing the accuracy of diagnosing DON and its early stages.

title: Facial emotion recognition of sadness relates to superior parietal gray matter volume in mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is associated with early, regionally selective neurodegenerative changes that may affect socioemotional functioning before atrophy becomes widespread. This study examined whether structural brain alterations in MCI relate to facial emotion recognition performance. Sixty adults (30 MCI, 30 healthy controls), aged 50-86 years, completed neuropsychological testing, the Facial emotion composite Task, and structural MRI. Whole-brain voxel-based morphometry revealed no significant gray matter volume differences between groups. However, targeted region-of-interest ROI analyses demonstrated lower right amygdala and bilateral hippocampal volumes in patients with MCI. Cortical thickness analyses identified two regions with lower thickness in MCI: the right superior parietal lobule and the left posterior insula. A significant Group × Sadness interaction indicated that the association between left superior parietal gray matter volume and sadness recognition differed between groups. Follow-up analyses of the extracted values showed a positive association in MCI, although this within-group association did not reach statistical significance, and a significant inverse association in HCs. These findings suggest that early MCI involves selective thinning in association cortices supporting attention and salience processing. The sadness-specific interaction indicates that patients with MCI may rely on preserved superior parietal structure during sadness recognition, a pattern that is consistent with structural reserve accounts, although this interpretation remains speculative given the cross-sectional design.

title: Atypical Stafne bone defect: a systematic review.
abstract: Atypically located Stafne bone defects (SBDs) may be challenging to identify because they deviate from the typical posterior mandibular presentation. This systematic review aims to analyze and synthesize the radiographic, anatomical, and histological characteristics of atypically located SBDs reported in the literature and to assist clinicians in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science databases up to January 2026. Eligibility criteria included English-language case reports and case series describing atypically located Stafne bone defects (SBDs). Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed independently by two reviewers using an adapted assessment tool for case reports. Seventy studies encompassing 91 atypical cases were included. Atypically located SBDs were most frequently reported in the anterior mandible. Despite their variable localization, these defects share key anatomical and radiographic features with classical SBDs, including well-defined unilocular radiolucencies and lingual cortical depressions. Advanced imaging modalities, particularly cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), play an important role in confirming these features and in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. Histological analysis, when available, most commonly revealed normal salivary gland tissue without evidence of neoplastic transformation. Atypically located SBDs demonstrate consistent radiographic and anatomical characteristics that may assist clinicians in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. This review improves the understanding of this under-recognized anatomical variant and highlights the importance of appropriate imaging evaluation in ambiguous cases. Recognition of these features may facilitate accurate diagnosis and help avoid unnecessary invasive procedures.

title: Predictive factors associated with interval changes in STN-DBS lead-tip position between immediate and delayed postoperative CT.
abstract: Brain shift during deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery may contribute to changes in lead position. Although intracranial air volume is considered an important factor, other intraoperative factors may also influence lead displacement. This study evaluated interval changes in subthalamic nucleus (STN)-DBS lead-tip position between immediate and delayed postoperative computed tomography (CT) and investigated factors associated with these changes, including intracranial air volume and intraoperative head position. We retrospectively analyzed 42 DBS leads implanted bilaterally in the STN of 21 patients with Parkinson's disease. Lead-tip coordinates were assessed using Elements software (Brainlab) on CT obtained immediately after implantation and after resolution of intracranial air. Interval displacement was defined as the difference in lead-tip coordinates between the delayed and immediate postoperative CT scans. Intraoperative head position was quantified as "Angle A," measured from the horizontal reference line to the anterior commissure-posterior commissure line. Associations between potential explanatory factors and lead-tip displacement were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with patient included as a random intercept to account for within-patient correlation between bilateral leads. Lead-tip positions showed significant interval displacement in the lateral, anterior, and caudal directions. In univariable mixed-effects analysis, intracranial air volume was significantly associated with anterior displacement (β = 0.033, 95% CI 0.018-0.048, p < 0.001), whereas Angle A was not (β = -0.030, 95% CI - 0.067-0.007, p = 0.111). In a multivariable mixed-effects model including intracranial air volume and Angle A, intracranial air volume remained significantly associated with anterior displacement (β = 0.0289, 95% CI 0.0110-0.0469, p = 0.002), while a larger Angle A was associated with less anterior displacement (β = -0.0270, 95% CI - 0.0535 to - 0.0004, p = 0.047). Intracranial air volume was consistently associated with anterior STN-DBS lead-tip displacement between immediate and delayed postoperative CT. Intraoperative head position was also associated with anterior displacement after adjustment for intracranial air volume, although this finding was of borderline statistical significance and should be considered exploratory. These findings support efforts to minimize intracranial air entry during DBS implantation, while the potential influence of intraoperative head positioning requires further prospective investigation.

title: THINKERS-X: multisequence MRI radiomics in a mixture-of-experts model for outcome prediction and exploratory dose-scenario evaluation in lung cancer brain metastases treated with radiosurgery.
abstract: We developed THINKERS-X: Lung, the eXtended multimodal evolution of THINKERS-Lung, to determine whether multisequence MRI radiomics provides incremental value for lesion-specific outcome prediction and exploratory dose-scenario evaluation after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for lung cancer brain metastases. We performed a retrospective single-center study of 767 patients with 3,728 lung cancer brain metastases treated with GKRS. THINKERS-X preserved the original mixture-of-experts and discrete-time survival architecture while adding a dedicated computational neuroradiology expert. Approximately 2,400 radiomic features per metastasis were extracted from pretreatment FSPGR/T1-weighted postcontrast, T2-weighted, and SWAN MRI. Validation used patient-grouped 5-fold cross-validation and a completely closed patient-grouped internal holdout cohort. In grouped cross-validation, THINKERS-X achieved a mean AUC12 of 0.919 ± 0.021 versus 0.876 for THINKERS-Lung (paired difference, 0.043; 95% CI 0.026-0.061; p < 0.001). In the internal holdout cohort, AUC12 improved from 0.863 to 0.929 (95% CI 0.895-0.958), with a paired difference of 0.066 (95% CI 0.031-0.101; p < 0.001). Mean absolute error decreased from 1.26 to 0.84 months. The calibrated Brier score was 0.039, calibration slope 0.94, and intercept 0.04. Radiomics altered model-derived dose-response profiles in 30.0% of metastases and the model-ranked candidate dose in 23.9%. THINKERS-X improved lesion-specific longitudinal prediction, temporal accuracy, and probabilistic calibration beyond THINKERS-Lung while materially altering exploratory dose-scenario evaluation in a subset of metastases. External multicenter and prospective validation are required before clinical implementation.

title: Postoperative DWI morphology and neurological worsening after eloquent-area glioma surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Purpose To assess whether the association between postoperative diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and neurological worsening after eloquent-area glioma surgery differs according to lesion morphology. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 139 consecutive patients undergoing resection of eloquent-area supratentorial gliomas (WHO 2-4). Postoperative MRI (< 48 h) classified lesions as sector- or rim-shaped. Neurological status was assessed at discharge and 4-6 months. Results DWI lesions occurred in 44/139 patients (31.7%; 31 sector-shaped, 13 rim-shaped); 59 (42.4%) worsened at discharge. Overall, DWI positivity alone was not associated with worsening. Sector-shaped DWI lesions were associated with neurological worsening (positive predictive value, PPV of 58.1%) and remained associated after multivariable adjustment (OR 3.83, 95% CI 1.30-11.29), although the confidence interval was wide and the unadjusted association was borderline. Rim-shaped lesions carried a PPV of 38.5%, comparable to the risk in DWI-negative patients (37.9%), and the two morphologies did not differ significantly in direct comparison. Awake craniotomy was also independently associated with worsening, and frontal site with a lower risk. 61% of worsening occurred with negative DWI. A deficit was present at the 4-6 month follow-up in 9 patients (6.5%), all with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, and was associated with a ≥ 50% evoked-potential decrease. Conclusion In this cohort, postoperative DWI positivity was associated with neurological worsening mainly when the lesion was sector-shaped, a finding that requires confirmation in larger series. Rim-shaped lesions showed a risk of worsening similar to that of a negative scan. Most worsening occurs without DWI ischemia, suggesting non-ischemic mechanisms of function-guided surgery. A deficit at follow-up occurred only in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and was associated with intraoperative neurophysiological changes.

title: Improving the fairness and robustness of deep learning classification models through bias mitigation and post hoc calibration.
abstract: The goal of this study was to enhance the fairness and clinical applicability of deep learning models for classifying Alzheimer's disease from structural MRI scans. To achieve this, we addressed two key challenges: age-related bias and unreliable probability estimates. Specifically, we investigated in-processing debiasing strategies to achieve age-invariant predictions while preserving diagnostic accuracy. We also systematically evaluated post hoc calibration methods to improve the reliability, interpretability, and clinical usefulness of predicted probabilities across diverse patient populations. Structural MRI data from three independent cohorts (ADNI, AIBL, and DELCODE) were preprocessed using a standardized pipeline. Age-related bias was addressed using two in-processing strategies, adversarial training (CF-Net) and GLM-based feature residualization (PMDN), implemented in a shared 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) framework. Additionally, post hoc calibration was performed using four regression methods: logistic, probit, isotonic, and Bayesian binning. We evaluated model performance, fairness, and calibration using classification as well as calibration-specific metrics. PMDN achieved the best overall performance, with higher balanced accuracy (0.71) and improved calibration (Brier ≈ 0.22), showing substantially reduced variability compared to baseline and CF-Net. PMDN effectively removed age-related bias, achieving near-zero age prediction correlation; CF-Net, however, showed only partial and unstable debiasing. Post hoc calibration further improved probability reliability, with nonparametric methods (isotonic regression and Bayesian binning) yielding the lowest calibration errors (MCE ≈ 0.21-0.24). This study shows that, although deep learning models achieve similar classification performance, they differ significantly in terms of calibration, stability, and fairness. PMDN provides more consistent and effective age bias mitigation than the CF-Net approach, particularly in clinically relevant subgroups. Post hoc calibration improves probability reliability further, with nonparametric methods achieving the best calibration.

PMDN achieved the best overall performance, with higher balanced accuracy (0.71) and improved calibration (Brier ≈ 0.22), showing substantially reduced variability compared to baseline and CF-Net. PMDN effectively removed age-related bias, achieving near-zero age prediction correlation; CF-Net, however, showed only partial and unstable debiasing. Post hoc calibration further improved probability reliability, with nonparametric methods (isotonic regression and Bayesian binning) yielding the lowest calibration errors (MCE ≈ 0.21-0.24). This study shows that, although deep learning models achieve similar classification performance, they differ significantly in terms of calibration, stability, and fairness. PMDN provides more consistent and effective age bias mitigation than the CF-Net approach, particularly in clinically relevant subgroups. Post hoc calibration improves probability reliability further, with nonparametric methods achieving the best calibration.

title: MRI and proton MR spectroscopy in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a comprehensive imaging review.
abstract: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) remains a leading cause of neonatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental disability. Although cranial ultrasound is widely used as a bedside screening tool, brain MRI has become central to diagnosis, injury pattern classification, timing estimation, and outcome prediction. Furthermore, proton MR spectroscopy ( 1 H-MRS) provides complementary metabolic biomarkers that enhance prognostication. This review focuses on MRI and 1 H-MRS in neonatal encephalopathy due to hypoxic-ischemic injury, addressing both term and preterm infants. The pathophysiologic determinants of injury distribution are summarized, the optimal timing of imaging and diffusion evolution is discussed, and practical acquisition protocols including recommended sequences and 1 H-MRS parameters are proposed. Key MRI phenotypes in term infants-basal ganglia-thalamus injury, watershed/parasagittal cortical-subcortical injury, and global or near-total injury patterns are reviewed with attention to common pitfalls such as diffusion pseudonormalization and evolving T1/T2 signal changes. For preterm infants, this review highlights distinctive vulnerabilities of the germinal matrix and periventricular white matter, emphasizing the spectrum from punctate white matter injury (WMI) to cystic periventricular leukomalacia (PVL). For 1 H-MRS, voxel selection, echo time considerations, and interpretation of lactate, N-acetylaspartate (NAA), choline, creatine, and myo-inositol are detailed. Evidence suggests that deep gray matter lactate/NAA or NAA-based metrics serve as reliable and robust outcome biomarkers. Emerging directions including arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion are also discussed.

title: Comparison of PMAneo and RAPID in acute ischemic stroke: agreement in CT perfusion analysis and DEFUSE 3 imaging eligibility.
abstract: Automated computed tomography perfusion (CTP) analysis plays a key role in triaging acute ischemic stroke (AIS). This study aimed to evaluate the agreement of PMAneo compared with RAPID in a multicenter setting. We retrospectively reviewed 99 patients with anterior circulation AIS from three stroke centers using four different CT scanners. CTP data were processed using both PMAneo and RAPID. Volumetric agreement for ischemic core volume and Tmax > 6 s volume was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with volume discrepancies. EVT imaging eligibility was evaluated according to the DEFUSE 3 criteria (ischemic core volume < 70 mL, mismatch ratio ≥ 1.8, and absolute mismatch volume ≥ 15 mL), using RAPID as the comparator. Ischemic core volumes showed excellent agreement between the two platforms (ICC = 0.881, 95% CI 0.827-0.918), and Tmax > 6 s volumes showed good agreement (ICC = 0.761, 95% CI 0.283-0.896), whereas mismatch volumes showed moderate agreement (ICC = 0.661, 95% CI 0.146-0.844). For the ischemic core threshold (< 70 mL), PMAneo demonstrated 100% (95% CI 96-100%) relative sensitivity and 67% (95% CI 38-88%) relative specificity. For the full DEFUSE 3 criteria, the relative sensitivity and specificity were 81% (95% CI 70-89%) and 84% (95% CI 66-95%), respectively. Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated proportional bias, with PMAneo underestimating volumes relative to RAPID as lesion size increased. Basal ganglia involvement and imaging site were significantly associated with these volume differences (p < 0.05). PMAneo showed high volumetric agreement and comparable DEFUSE 3 imaging eligibility to RAPID, suggesting it is a reliable alternative for automated CTP analysis. Although proportional bias and potential diagnostic discrepancies were observed in borderline cases near clinically relevant thresholds, PMAneo may facilitate broader access to automated CTP analysis.

title: MRI-defined parametrial venous invasion in locally advanced cervical cancer: association with pathological venous invasion, pretreatment lymph node metastasis, and survival outcomes.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate MRI-defined parametrial venous invasion (mrPMVI) for detecting pathological parametrial venous invasion (pPMVI) and its associations with pretreatment lymph node metastasis (LNM) and survival outcomes in locally advanced cervical cancer. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 42 patients with cervical cancer with parametrial invasion on MRI or histopathology, corresponding to International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2018 stage IIB or higher disease. Fifteen patients underwent surgery without preoperative therapy and were included in the pathological validation analysis. Image interpretation was primarily based on T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging. Two radiologists independently assessed mrPMVI using a five-point scoring system. Scores ≥ 3 were predefined as mrPMVI-positive. Diagnostic performance for pPMVI and interobserver agreement were evaluated. Univariable logistic and Cox regression analyses were performed for pretreatment LNM and survival outcomes, respectively. Results pPMVI was present in 10 of 15 patients. The five-point mrPMVI score showed an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.87 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.60-0.98) for detecting pPMVI. The predefined threshold (≥ 3) yielded 30.0% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Interobserver agreement for the five-point mrPMVI score was substantial (linearly weighted κ = 0.75). mrPMVI positivity was associated with pretreatment LNM (odds ratio = 4.00, 95% CI: 1.05-15.26, p = 0.042). During a median follow-up of 24.0 months, 16 patients experienced disease progression and 10 died. mrPMVI positivity was associated with shorter progression-free survival (hazard ratio = 34.25, 95% CI: 4.35-269.91; p < 0.001) and overall survival (hazard ratio = 10.16; 95% CI: 1.28-80.61, p = 0.028). Conclusion The mrPMVI score showed potential for identifying pPMVI, although the predefined threshold was highly specific but insensitive. mrPMVI positivity was associated with pretreatment LNM and survival outcomes, suggesting potential complementary value for risk characterization in locally advanced cervical cancer.

Purpose

This retrospective study included 42 patients with cervical cancer with parametrial invasion on MRI or histopathology, corresponding to International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2018 stage IIB or higher disease. Fifteen patients underwent surgery without preoperative therapy and were included in the pathological validation analysis. Image interpretation was primarily based on T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging. Two radiologists independently assessed mrPMVI using a five-point scoring system. Scores ≥ 3 were predefined as mrPMVI-positive. Diagnostic performance for pPMVI and interobserver agreement were evaluated. Univariable logistic and Cox regression analyses were performed for pretreatment LNM and survival outcomes, respectively.

Results

pPMVI was present in 10 of 15 patients. The five-point mrPMVI score showed an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.87 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.60-0.98) for detecting pPMVI. The predefined threshold (≥ 3) yielded 30.0% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Interobserver agreement for the five-point mrPMVI score was substantial (linearly weighted κ = 0.75). mrPMVI positivity was associated with pretreatment LNM (odds ratio = 4.00, 95% CI: 1.05-15.26, p = 0.042). The mrPMVI score showed potential for identifying pPMVI, although the predefined threshold was highly specific but insensitive. mrPMVI positivity was associated with pretreatment LNM and survival outcomes, suggesting potential complementary value for risk characterization in locally advanced cervical cancer.

title: A Hybrid Human-AI Workflow for Ultrasound Report Quality Control: A Multicenter Performance and Efficiency Evaluation.
abstract: This study evaluated a hybrid human-AI workflow for ultrasound report quality assurance using multicenter retrospective data. 786 anonymized ultrasound reports covering 22 examination categories were collected from four hospitals. Reports containing naturally occurring or implanted errors were matched across arms. GPT-4o and DeepSeek-v3 performed initial screening before review by six human reviewers (HRs). HR with blinded expert over-reading (HR-ex) served as control. Accuracy, false-positive (FP) and false-negative (FN) rates, and review time were compared. Supplementary validation compared HR and DeepSeek-assisted review using 1680 consecutive reports without implanted errors. Hybrid workflow (HYB) accuracy was comparable to HR (4o-HYB 80.2%, v3-HYB 82.5%, HR 82.3%) but lower than HR-ex (87.3%). Both HYBs showed higher FN rates than HR-ex (4o-HYB 34.2% and v3-HYB 27.3% vs HR-ex 16.9%, both p < 0.001). Severity assessment did not indicate preferential omission of clinically significant errors. Human verification reduced LLM-generated FNs and FPs. Median review time decreased substantially from 51.0 s (HR-ex) to 11.0 s (4o-HYB) and 12.0 s (v3-HYB). In supplementary validation (error prevalence, 9.6%), v3.2-HYB and HR showed FN rates of 22.6% and 24.3%, FP rates of 7.7% and 10.0%, and median review times of 15.4 and 24.3 s, respectively. The LLM-assisted HYB achieved accuracy comparable to single-physician review while substantially reducing audit time. These findings require prospective real-world validation before routine clinical implementation.

title: A natural neuronal receptor-derived MRI probe targets β-amyloid oligomers for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Early-to-mid detection of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains challenging because clinically used amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) probes primarily visualize fibrillar β-amyloid (Aβ) deposits and require radioactive isotopes. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers a radiation-free alternative, but its application in molecular AD diagnosis is limited by insufficient blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and poor specificity toward early-to-mid Aβ species. Here, we developed a BBB-crossing liposomal MRI probe, Lipo@D1D2-Gd, by integrating a natural Aβ oligomer-binding receptor domain with a gadolinium chelator. The extracellular D1D2 domains of human leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor B2 (LilrB2), a neuronal receptor that recognizes neurotoxic Aβ oligomers, were recombinantly produced and bioorthogonally conjugated with a gadolinium chelator. The resulting D1D2-Gd retained its Aβ-binding capability and MRI contrast activity. To enable brain delivery, D1D2-Gd was encapsulated within maltose-functionalized PEGylated liposomes designed to facilitate BBB transport. After intravenous administration to 4-month-old 5xFAD mice, Lipo@D1D2-Gd crossed the BBB, accumulated in Aβ-rich brain regions, and generated MRI contrast enhancement that differentiated 5xFAD mice from wild-type controls. Systemic safety evaluation showed no obvious hematological, biochemical, or histological toxicity. This study establishes a receptor-derived, BBB-crossing biomaterial platform for radiation-free molecular imaging of early-to-mid AD-associated Aβ pathology. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: 1) Promising Targeting Strategy: We repurposed a human-derived natural receptor domain (LilrB2 D1D2) as a targeting module for β-amyloid (Aβ) oligomers, a key pathogenic species in Alzheimer's disease (AD). 2) Non-invasive MRI Approach: We constructed a liposomal probe designed to deliver the Gd-labeled targeting agent to the brain, enabling the detection of Aβ-associated pathology in 4-month-old 5xFAD mice via non-radioactive MRI, well before overt cognitive decline. 3) Experimental Validation: We demonstrate the probe's association with Aβ oligomers/plaques, effective BBB crossing, differences in MRI signals between AD model and wild-type mice, and an initially favorable biosafety profile, with no observed toxicity under the tested conditions. 4) Clinical Translation Potential: Our work presents a promising pathway toward a safe, accessible, and early-to-mid-stage AD screening tool, with the potential to facilitate population-wide screening and earlier therapeutic intervention.

title: Contralateral piriform cortex alterations after surgery for temporal lobe epilepsy: A pilot MRI volumetry study.
abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is increasingly conceptualized as a network disorder, with the piriform cortex as an implicated region. We characterized postoperative contralateral piriform cortex-cortical amygdala (PCA) structural and perfusion-related changes in a small seizure-free TLE cohort. Nine patients with drug-resistant TLE who underwent epilepsy surgery and achieved postoperative seizure freedom were included in this single-center pre-post pilot study. Bilateral PCA was manually delineated on 3D T1-weighted MRI using ITK-SNAP, and volumes were normalized to total intracranial volume derived from CAT12 segmentation. Eight atlas-derived contralateral temporal lobe regions were examined as exploratory regional-specificity comparisons. In patients with available pulsed arterial spin labeling (PASL), piriform and putaminal signal intensities were measured by region-of-interest analysis. Non-parametric paired tests were used; secondary and exploratory analyses were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Normalized to total intracranial volume (TIV) contralateral PCA volume decreased postoperatively (Wilcoxon Z = -2.073, exact two-tailed p = 0.039; r = 0.69). None of the eight atlas-derived contralateral temporal regions showed a significant pre-post volume change. Contralateral putamen-normalized piriform signal intensity did not change significantly (Z = -0.105, p = 0.917), and no secondary or exploratory analysis remained significant after FDR correction. In this hypothesis-generating pilot cohort, contralateral PCA volume decreased after epilepsy surgery, whereas the PASL-derived signal-intensity measure did not show a corresponding group-level change. These observations do not establish a surgery-induced network mechanism and require confirmation in larger controlled longitudinal cohorts.

title: Bicentric comparison of 3-year clinical outcomes between endoscopic ultrasound-guided embolization with coil and hemostatic adjunct versus balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration for treatment of bleeding gastric varices: A propensity-score matched study.
abstract: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided coil injection (EUS-COIL) and balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration (BRTO) performed by interventional radiology (IR) are both effective obliterative procedures to treat gastric varices. Comparative studies are lacking. Our aim was to assess clinical outcomes for EUS-COIL versus BRTO for treatment of acute gastric variceal bleeding. This retrospective cohort study included all patients admitted to two tertiary care centers between 2009-2024 who underwent either EUS-COIL or BRTO for bleeding gastric varices. The primary outcomes were technical/clinical success and adverse events. Secondary outcomes included transfusions, reintervention, length of hospital stay, further hepatic decompensation (esophageal variceal hemorrhage, new ascites, or new hepatic encephalopathy (HE)), and all-cause mortality. Subgroup analyses were performed in patients with cirrhosis, including with propensity score matching (PSM) which was conducted 1:1 for age, sex, Child-Pugh classification, MELD-Na score, and hemoglobin level on admission. Outcomes over the 36-months post-intervention were assessed using time-to-event analysis. A total of 94 patients were included (48 EUS-COIL, 46 BRTO), of whom 60 patients with cirrhosis (30 per group) were analyzed after propensity score matching. In the matched cohort, technical success was 100% in both groups and clinical success was 100% versus 93.3% (p=0.49). The EUS-COIL group experienced significantly fewer adverse events (3% vs 37%; p=0.003) and had a longer time-to-reintervention (65 ± 52 days vs 10 ± 9.6 days; p=0.022) over a median follow-up 900 ± 790 days. The incidence of further hepatic decompensation was lower in the EUS-COIL group (10% vs 40%; p=0.007), as was the likelihood of further hepatic decompensation (HR 0.28 (95%CI: 0.08-0.984), p = 0.047) compared to BRTO. No significant differences were observed with regard to post-procedural transfusion requirements, rates of reintervention, length of hospital stay, and mortality in cirrhosis patients. In the unmatched cohort, technical (100% vs 80%; p=0.001) and clinical (100% vs 89%; p=0.03) success were higher with EUS-COIL than BRTO. In patients with gastric variceal hemorrhage, EUS-COIL demonstrated higher rates of technical/clinical success and lower rates of adverse events (both peri-procedural and on long-term follow-up) compared to BRTO. EUS-COIL had significantly lower rates of further hepatic decompensation. While larger prospective studies are required, these data suggest that EUS-COIL, when available, may be the preferred initial therapy for bleeding gastric varices as part of a step-up strategy.
