title: The role of cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement in patients with acute cardiac symptoms and troponin elevation in the era of high-sensitivity assays.
abstract: Objectives Diagnostic workup of patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no acute myocardial infarction (AMI) criteria is challenging. Cardiac CT angiography (CCTA) rules out obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). Adding late iodine enhancement and extracellular volume fraction (CCTA + LIE/ECV) provides insights into myocardial injury. However, the impact on working diagnosis, agreement with discharge diagnosis, and mid-term safety of implementing CCTA + LIE/ECV in the emergency department remains uncertain. Materials and methods Prospective study on consecutive patients presenting, from June 2018 to February 2025, with acute chest pain or equivalents, elevated troponin, and no AMI diagnosis, excluding previously revascularized patients. Patients underwent CCTA to rule out obstructive CAD (≥ 50% stenosis). CCTA-negative patients underwent myocardial tissue characterization with LIE; if negative, ECV was quantified. Primary endpoint modification of working diagnosis by CT. Secondary endpoints: agreement between CT and discharge diagnoses after standard-of-care assessment; mid-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) in CT-negative patients. Results Among 191 patients (age 70 [55-79] years; 53% men), CCTA identified obstructive CAD in 76/191 (40%). LIE/ECV were positive in 58/106 (55%) of CCTA-negative cases, revealing myocarditis in 32/106 (30%), AMI with non-obstructive CAD in 8/106 (8%), Takotsubo in 14/106 (13%), amyloidosis in 3/106 (3%), and dilated cardiomyopathy in 1/106 (1%). CT modified the working diagnosis in 91/191 (48%) patients. Agreement between CT and discharge diagnosis was 0.94 (95% CI 0.89-0.97). In patients with negative CCTA + LIE/ECV, no MACEs occurred after 24 [interquartile range, 19-29] months. Conclusion In patients with acute symptoms, elevated troponin, and no AMI, a protocol combining CCTA + LIE/ECV enables etiologic assessment of coronary and myocardial conditions, refines working diagnosis, and entails a favorable prognosis when negative. Key points Question Patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no evidence of acute myocardial infarction represent a diagnostic challenge: cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement may have diagnostic and prognostic implications. Findings CT angiography with late iodine enhancement provided a diagnosis in 75% of patients and modified the working diagnosis in 48%. In the 25% CT-negative patients, no adverse events occurred at mid-term follow-up. Clinical relevance A CT protocol including coronary artery evaluation and myocardial tissue characterization may provide a rapid etiological diagnosis in patients with acute symptoms and troponin elevation, potentially supporting earlier clinical decision-making and reducing the need for additional downstream testing.
originalAbstract:
Objectives

Diagnostic workup of patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no acute myocardial infarction (AMI) criteria is challenging. Cardiac CT angiography (CCTA) rules out obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). Adding late iodine enhancement and extracellular volume fraction (CCTA + LIE/ECV) provides insights into myocardial injury. However, the impact on working diagnosis, agreement with discharge diagnosis, and mid-term safety of implementing CCTA + LIE/ECV in the emergency department remains uncertain.

Materials and methods

Prospective study on consecutive patients presenting, from June 2018 to February 2025, with acute chest pain or equivalents, elevated troponin, and no AMI diagnosis, excluding previously revascularized patients. Patients underwent CCTA to rule out obstructive CAD (≥ 50% stenosis). CCTA-negative patients underwent myocardial tissue characterization with LIE; if negative, ECV was quantified.

Primary endpoint

modification of working diagnosis by CT. Secondary endpoints: agreement between CT and discharge diagnoses after standard-of-care assessment; mid-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) in CT-negative patients.

Results

Among 191 patients (age 70 [55-79] years; 53% men), CCTA identified obstructive CAD in 76/191 (40%). LIE/ECV were positive in 58/106 (55%) of CCTA-negative cases, revealing myocarditis in 32/106 (30%), AMI with non-obstructive CAD in 8/106 (8%), Takotsubo in 14/106 (13%), amyloidosis in 3/106 (3%), and dilated cardiomyopathy in 1/106 (1%). CT modified the working diagnosis in 91/191 (48%) patients. Agreement between CT and discharge diagnosis was 0.94 (95% CI 0.89-0.97). In patients with negative CCTA + LIE/ECV, no MACEs occurred after 24 [interquartile range, 19-29] months.

Conclusion

In patients with acute symptoms, elevated troponin, and no AMI, a protocol combining CCTA + LIE/ECV enables etiologic assessment of coronary and myocardial conditions, refines working diagnosis, and entails a favorable prognosis when negative.

Key points

Question Patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no evidence of acute myocardial infarction represent a diagnostic challenge: cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement may have diagnostic and prognostic implications. Findings CT angiography with late iodine enhancement provided a diagnosis in 75% of patients and modified the working diagnosis in 48%. In the 25% CT-negative patients, no adverse events occurred at mid-term follow-up. Clinical relevance A CT protocol including coronary artery evaluation and myocardial tissue characterization may provide a rapid etiological diagnosis in patients with acute symptoms and troponin elevation, potentially supporting earlier clinical decision-making and reducing the need for additional downstream testing.

title: Low-dose vs standard-dose photon-counting CT for myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease: a prospective feasibility study.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the clinical utility of photon counting computed tomography (PCCT)-derived quantitative parameters for assessing interstitial lung disease (ILD) burden in patients with inflammatory idiopathic myopathy (IIM), comparing standard-dose (SD) and tin-filtered low-dose (LD) protocols, and to assess the added value of ultrathin reconstructions. Materials and methods In this single-centre prospective study (September 2023-November 2024), outpatients with IIM-ILD underwent two consecutive PCCT scans. Quantitative ILD features were extracted using a commercial deep-learning software (ContextFlow ADVANCE Chest CT). Primary analyses compared LD 1.0 mm with SD 1.0 mm reconstructions using Bland-Altman analysis, with exploratory analyses of ultrathin (0.4 mm) reconstructions. Correlation analyses between deep learning-derived quantitative parameters, visual assessment, and pulmonary function tests were performed. Results Forty-eight adults with IIM-ILD (40 females; mean age, 53.88 ± 11.13 years) were included. The LD protocol achieved a substantial dose reduction (CTDIvol: 0.77 vs 5.40 mGy) while maintaining good agreement with SD (mean net differences [MNDs] < 1% for all patterns). LD-1.0 mm protocol yielded higher volume of ground-glass opacity (MND, 0.98%) and lower volume of fibrosis extent (MND, -0.64%). Reticular pattern showed strong association with FVC% (rho SD1.0mm = -0.62, p < 0.001) and DLCO% (rho SD1.0mm = -0.73, p < 0.001), with similar correlations observed under LD acquisition (Δrho ≤ 0.02). Ultrathin reconstructions yielded greater measurement of bronchiectasis (MND, 0.13% on SD scans). Conclusion LD PCCT serves as a radiation-sparing alternative for quantitative disease assessment. Ultrathin reconstructions provide limited additional value. Future longitudinal studies are warranted to validate the performance of LD PCCT for disease monitoring. Key points Question Can LD photon-counting CT provide robust quantitative assessment of ILD burden in patients with inflammatory myopathy compared with SD imaging? Findings Deep learning segmentation yielded LD ILD patterns that closely matched SD results, with all MNDs below 1%. Clinical relevance LD PCCT maintains quantitative robustness and physiological validity for IIM-ILD assessment, with total disease burden showing good agreement with the SD protocol, offering a radiation-sparing alternative without compromising CT-physiology correlation.
originalAbstract:
Objectives

To evaluate the clinical utility of photon counting computed tomography (PCCT)-derived quantitative parameters for assessing interstitial lung disease (ILD) burden in patients with inflammatory idiopathic myopathy (IIM), comparing standard-dose (SD) and tin-filtered low-dose (LD) protocols, and to assess the added value of ultrathin reconstructions.

Materials and methods

In this single-centre prospective study (September 2023-November 2024), outpatients with IIM-ILD underwent two consecutive PCCT scans. Quantitative ILD features were extracted using a commercial deep-learning software (ContextFlow ADVANCE Chest CT). Primary analyses compared LD 1.0 mm with SD 1.0 mm reconstructions using Bland-Altman analysis, with exploratory analyses of ultrathin (0.4 mm) reconstructions. Correlation analyses between deep learning-derived quantitative parameters, visual assessment, and pulmonary function tests were performed.

Results

Forty-eight adults with IIM-ILD (40 females; mean age, 53.88 ± 11.13 years) were included. The LD protocol achieved a substantial dose reduction (CTDIvol: 0.77 vs 5.40 mGy) while maintaining good agreement with SD (mean net differences [MNDs] < 1% for all patterns). LD-1.0 mm protocol yielded higher volume of ground-glass opacity (MND, 0.98%) and lower volume of fibrosis extent (MND, -0.64%). Reticular pattern showed strong association with FVC% (rhoSD1.0mm = -0.62, p < 0.001) and DLCO% (rhoSD1.0mm = -0.73, p < 0.001), with similar correlations observed under LD acquisition (Δrho ≤ 0.02). Ultrathin reconstructions yielded greater measurement of bronchiectasis (MND, 0.13% on SD scans).

Conclusion

LD PCCT serves as a radiation-sparing alternative for quantitative disease assessment. Ultrathin reconstructions provide limited additional value. Future longitudinal studies are warranted to validate the performance of LD PCCT for disease monitoring.

Key points

Question Can LD photon-counting CT provide robust quantitative assessment of ILD burden in patients with inflammatory myopathy compared with SD imaging? Findings Deep learning segmentation yielded LD ILD patterns that closely matched SD results, with all MNDs below 1%. Clinical relevance LD PCCT maintains quantitative robustness and physiological validity for IIM-ILD assessment, with total disease burden showing good agreement with the SD protocol, offering a radiation-sparing alternative without compromising CT-physiology correlation.

title: Retinal layer thickness as a potential marker for future cardiovascular events - a UK Biobank cohort study using optical coherence tomography.
abstract: Aims Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide. For CVD prevention, effective screening is needed to identify high-risk individuals. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides a noninvasive, low-cost "quick look" into the brain and has recently shown thinning of certain retinal layers in patients with previous CVD. We explored if OCT-derived retinal layer thicknesses could predict future major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: stroke/myocardial infarction/cardiovascular death). Methods In this retrospective cohort study, data of 51,293 participants from the UK Biobank were analyzed. We used cause-specific hazard models to evaluate the association of retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (RNFL) and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thickness with incident MACE, adjusting models for cardiovascular risk factors (CVRF) and performed subanalyses for association with incident stroke and myocardial infarction. Results Median follow-up time was 14.7 years. Both RNFL thickness (aHR 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, p < 0.001) and GCIPL thickness (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.92-1.00, p = 0.04) were statistically associated with incident MACE in cause-specific hazard models adjusted for CVRF. Interestingly, RNFL thickness was more strongly associated with incident myocardial infarction (aHR 0.94, 95% CI 0.88-0.99, p = 0.02) while GCIPL was more strongly associated with incident stroke (aHR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.96, p = 0.003). Conclusion RNFL and GCIPL thicknesses are associated with future MACE, even after adjusting for CVRF. OCT-measured retinal layer thickness could contribute to the assessment of cardiovascular risk.

title: MR spectroscopy in the diagnosis of lumbar discogenic pain.
abstract: Purpose to determine whether magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) provides similar clinical data to low pressure provocative discography (PD). Methods Twenty patients suffering from axial lower back pain underwent both MRS and PD concurrently. MRS was performed on a Siemens 3T scanner* of the lower three lumbar discs, where possible. Collapsed discs could not be assessed. Low pressure PD was performed on at least the lower three discs, by the author with considerable experience of the technique. Results MRS agreed with PD findings in 70-87% of 55 discs tested, depending on the agreement level set. Of the non-agreements, 10/17 were under-calls, 3 were overcalls and 4 were indeterminate. Conclusion MRS of lumbar discs may become a viable alternative to PD, as our experience and the technique evolves.

title: Automated 3D Analysis of Hip Morphology in a Young Adult Population.
abstract: Purpose Although many factors contribute to the development of hip OA, structural findings, such as acetabular dysplasia, are recognized as strong contributing factors to early degenerative changes. However, conventional two-dimensional imaging cannot fully capture the joint's three-dimensional anatomy. This study aimed to develop and validate an automated MRI-based method for 3D hip morphology analysis. Methods MRI data from 2,454 participants in the Generation R Cohort (1,199 males; 1,255 females; mean age 18.4 years; mean BMI 22.7 kg/m 2 ) were analyzed. An nnU-Net deep learning model, trained on 40 manually segmented hips, automatically segmented femoral bone, acetabular bone, and femoral and acetabular cartilage. Model performance was assessed using Dice scores. From the segmentations, five categories of morphological features were computed: basic geometric metrics, cartilage volumes, angular measurements, coverage metrics, and joint space width. Sex differences were evaluated using independent t-tests, and BMI-related differences using one-way ANOVA. Results The model achieved Dice scores of 0.97 for femoral bone, 0.90 for acetabular bone, 0.76 for femoral cartilage, and 0.77 for acetabular cartilage. Reference ranges were established for all biomarkers. Significant differences were observed between males and females and across BMI groups. Conclusion Automated 3D hip morphology analysis using MRI is feasible and reliable. The generated reference values enhance understanding of hip development and anatomical variation in young adults and support future large-scale, reproducible assessments. All developed code is made openly available at https://gitlab.com/radiology/msk/genr/hip/hip-segmentation-and-biomarkers.

title: Age-associated radiomic phenotyping in mice using multi-energy photon-counting and preclinical CT: an exploratory study.
abstract: To investigate whether CT-derived radiomic features capture imaging patterns associated with chronological age groups in mice and to assess the influence of imaging platform and photon-counting CT reconstruction strategy on classification performance. Female C57BL/6NRj mice from three chronological age groups (28, 88, and 99 weeks; n = 11) underwent clinical photon-counting CT (PCCT) and preclinical Albira II CT. Heart, liver, and spleen were segmented and radiomic features were extracted. The individual mouse was defined as the independent biological unit. Model development and evaluation used nested leave-one-mouse-out cross-validation with all preprocessing, feature selection, model selection, and, where applicable, reconstruction-energy selection restricted to the respective training folds. Organ-level class probabilities were averaged to generate one mouse-level prediction. Monoenergetic PCCT reconstructions from 40 to 180 keV were evaluated, including a fully nested energy-and-pipeline selection analysis. A grouped mouse-level permutation analysis with 200 permutations was performed for the primary monoenergetic workflow. Albira II correctly classified 5/11 mice (45.5%; 95% CI, 21.3-72.0%), whereas PCCT-SPP correctly classified 10/11 mice (90.9%; 95% CI, 62.3-98.4%). The fully nested monoenergetic PCCT workflow correctly classified 9/11 mice (81.8%; 95% CI, 52.3-94.9%; balanced accuracy, 83.3%; macro-F1, 83.3%). Energy-specific performance varied considerably: 110 keV showed the highest accuracy (81.8%) and was selected in 7/11 outer folds, whereas the highest macro one-vs-rest AUC occurred at 130 keV (0.867). None of the 200 permuted analyses reached the observed fully nested monoenergetic accuracy (plus-one corrected Monte-Carlo p = 0.005). CT-derived radiomic features showed chronological age-group-associated patterns in this exploratory murine cohort, with classification performance varying substantially across imaging platforms and reconstruction strategies. PCCT-SPP showed the numerically highest performance, while monoenergetic PCCT demonstrated pronounced energy dependence without evidence for a universally optimal reconstruction energy. These findings require validation in larger independent cohorts and correlation with independent biological-aging reference measures.

title: Diagnostic and Prognostic Value of Sonographic Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter in Patients with Ischemic Stroke or Hypertensive Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
abstract: Background Elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) is a critical complication in nontraumatic brain injury, yet invasive monitoring carries significant risks, and noninvasive alternatives remain undervalidated. Optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) ultrasonography represents a promising bedside technique, but data in nontraumatic populations are limited. This study evaluated the diagnostic and prognostic value of ONSD in neurocritical patients with ischemic stroke or hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage. Methods This prospective observational cohort study enrolled 100 neurocritical intensive care unit (ICU) patients with acute nontraumatic brain injury [ischemic stroke or hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage; Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) < 9] who underwent admission computed tomography (CT) and bedside ONSD ultrasonography. Sixty age- and sex-matched healthy volunteers were enrolled exclusively to provide descriptive reference values for physiological ONSD and were not included in the primary diagnostic or prognostic analyses. CT-based radiologic ICP surrogates were the reference standard. Exploratory analyses evaluated inter-eye variability, adjusted models, and in-hospital survival. Results ONSD increased stepwise across healthy controls, patients with negative CT, and patients with positive CT (4.62 ± 0.33, 5.52 ± 0.51, and 6.50 ± 0.51 mm, respectively). Among neurocritical patients, a cohort-derived cutoff of ≥ 6.00 mm yielded 86.7% sensitivity, 85.0% specificity, 89.7% positive predictive value, 81.0% negative predictive value, 86.0% accuracy, and 0.901 area under the curve (AUC). Above-threshold ONSD remained independently associated with CT-positive elevated ICP after adjustment for age, body mass index (BMI), GCS, and systolic blood pressure (SBP) in exploratory multivariable analysis. Exploratory survival analysis showed significantly higher in-hospital mortality in patients with ONSD above the cohort-derived threshold (log-rank p = 4.77 × 10 -13 ). Conclusions Bedside ultrasonographic ONSD measurement appears clinically useful for early triage and longitudinal bedside surveillance in neurocritical patients with ischemic stroke or hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage, particularly when invasive monitoring is unavailable or delayed.

title: Resistance Phenotypes and Treatment Sequencing After Immune Checkpoint Blockade in MSI-H/dMMR Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: A Review.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed microsatellite instability-high or mismatch repair-deficient metastatic colorectal cancer, but clinically relevant progression still occurs and treatment after progression remains undefined. We performed a clinically oriented narrative review, updated August 8, 2026, and separated direct prospective evidence, retrospective post-ICI evidence, extrapolation from general metastatic colorectal cancer trials, case-level evidence, and biological rationale. In the absence of prospective post-dual-ICI sequencing studies, we propose an evidence-informed conceptual framework. Apparent early progression should prompt confirmation of MSI/MMR status and exclusion of pseudoprogression before classification as early global progression, late systemic progression, or oligoprogression. BRAF V600E is common in MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer and is not an absolute predictor of ICI failure, but it is a major treatment-defining branch after progression. Repeat tissue biopsy or circulating tumor DNA profiling should be selective, used when findings can alter management and without delaying urgent therapy. ctDNA-based molecular residual disease is prognostic after curative-intent colorectal cancer resection, including metastasectomy, but is not validated to direct treatment of radiographically evident post-ICI progression. Oligoprogression warrants multidisciplinary consideration of local therapy, while ICI rechallenge remains investigational. Most recommendations are retrospective or extrapolated; transparent evidence boundaries and prospective post-dual-ICI studies are essential.

title: Mammography and Ultrasonography for Symptomatic Male Breast Lesions: A PRISMA-DTA Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Male breast disease is uncommon, but symptomatic men require reliable differentiation between benign conditions and lesions warranting biopsy or oncologic management. This PRISMA-DTA (Preferred Reporting Items for a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies) systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy, clinical utility, and evidentiary limitations of mammography and ultrasonography for malignant versus benign male breast lesions. Materials and methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus were searched from inception to May 30, 2026. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO before journal submission (CRD420261429183). Eligible reports evaluated mammography or ultrasonography in male breast disease and provided extractable 2 × 2 diagnostic data. Methodological quality was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized separately for each modality using bivariate random-effects modeling and summary receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results Thirteen eligible reports were included. Seven mammography datasets and five ultrasonography datasets were available for quantitative synthesis. Mammography showed a pooled sensitivity of 0.840 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.705-0.921) and a specificity of 0.951 (95% CI, 0.884-0.980), whereas ultrasonography showed a pooled sensitivity of 0.881 (95% CI, 0.775-0.941) and a specificity of 0.958 (95% CI, 0.869-0.987). Although pooled specificity estimates were high, their magnitude may have been influenced by heterogeneous diagnostic thresholds, differential verification, variable follow-up, and sparse malignant case counts. Nine of 13 reports were judged to have an overall high risk of bias, and consistent paired head-to-head data were lacking. Conclusion Current evidence supports mammography and ultrasonography as complementary tools in risk-stratified assessment of symptomatic male breast lesions. Pooled estimates should be interpreted cautiously because the evidence base is small and methodologically limited. Current data do not establish direct modality superiority, do not justify biopsy avoidance when clinical-imaging discordance persists, and do not determine the incremental value of routine combined imaging.

title: <sup>18</sup>F-Fluorodeoxyglucose PET in Rheumatologic and Autoimmune Disorders.
abstract: FDG PET detects the silent inflammation of autoimmune and rheumatologic diseases even before tissue damage, as activated leukocytes overexpress glucose transporters. It has an important role in large vessel vasculitis which includes early diagnosis, disease monitoring and response assessment to treatment. In inflammatory arthritides, it quantifies synovitis and enthesitis and detects early treatment response. In connective tissue and immunoglobulin G4 related diseases, whole body imaging maps silent disease, helps exclude malignancy, and guides biopsy. It is central to cardiac sarcoidosis and an early test in fever of unknown origin.

title: Interpretable CT-based radiomics nomogram integrating clinical and semantic features for preoperative grading of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms: a shap-based analysis.
abstract: Preoperative grading of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PNENs) is crucial for personalized management. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning framework based on CT imaging to predict PNENs pathological grades. We retrospectively analyzed 125 patients with pathologically confirmed PNENs, divided into training and test cohorts. A comprehensive radiomics pipeline was implemented, involving the extraction of high-dimensional features from CT images. We constructed three predictive models: a clinical model, a radiomics model, and a fusion model. To ensure methodological robustness, seven machine-learning algorithms were employed and cross-validated to identify the optimal classifier. Furthermore, the SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) method was utilized to decode the "black box" of the radiomics signature. The fusion model-integrating CT radiomic signatures with semantic hallmarks-consistently outperformed the standalone clinical and radiomics models, achieving a superior AUC of 0.891 in the validation cohort. SHAP analysis revealed that microscopic texture complexity (e.g., Zone Entropy) and macro-geometric irregularity (e.g., Sphericity) were the dominant predictors, aligning with the biological aggressiveness of high-grade lesions. By integrating multi-dimensional CT features with a rigorous machine-learning consensus, our study provides a highly accurate and interpretable "virtual biopsy" tool.

title: Core Descriptor Set for Studies Evaluating Interventions for Chronic Deep Venous Diseases.
abstract: Objective Chronic deep venous disease (CDVD) is a common and debilitating disease resulting in significant morbidity and costs. However, inconsistent reporting of patient characteristics in CDVD hinders study comparability and limits opportunities for data synthesis. This study aimed to develop a core descriptor set (CDS) for studies evaluating interventions for CDVD of the lower limbs. Methods Candidate descriptors were identified from published literature and stakeholder recommendations. Vascular surgeons, haematologists, interventional radiologists, and nurse specialists took part in two rounds of an international modified Delphi process using a nine point Likert scale to rank descriptor importance. Descriptors not meeting consensus criteria in the first round were re-evaluated in round two. Descriptors meeting the criteria for critical importance were discussed in a final meeting between international specialists to finalise the CDS. Results One hundred and thirty-eight Delphi participants were recruited from 29 countries. Ninety-eight descriptors were longlisted from the literature, refined to 84 by the steering group. After round one, 23 descriptors achieved consensus and were removed from subsequent rounds. Seven newly proposed descriptors were then added, resulting in a total of 68 descriptors in round two. Following round two, a further 13 descriptors achieved consensus with eight considered borderline. Following two Delphi survey rounds and a consensus meeting, 84 candidate descriptors were systematically evaluated and narrowed down to a final set of 21 core descriptors across the domains of demographics, thrombotic risk, venous history, anatomy, symptoms, and clinical findings. Conclusion This study defined the CDS for CDVD, facilitating more consistent, robust, and meaningful reporting across studies and enabling reliable synthesis.

title: Using Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance to Improve Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Risk Stratification in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes from Primary Care and Endocrinology Settings.
abstract: Objectives Current metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) guidelines recommend fibrosis screening in individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D) because of their increased risk of clinically significant fibrosis (≥F2). However, fibrosis risk is variable, and clinical tools to identify individuals at lower risk are lacking. We evaluated whether assessment of insulin resistance by homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) could improve risk stratification for clinically significant fibrosis. Methods We prospectively recruited 501 adults with T2D from primary care and endocrinology clinics. Participants were classified as insulin-resistant (HOMA-IR ≥2.5; n=350) or insulin-sensitive (HOMA-IR <2.5; n=151). Liver steatosis was assessed using VCTE, MRI/MRE, or liver biopsy according to the most accurate test, and the prevalence of clinically significant fibrosis (≥F2) was compared between groups. Results Insulin-resistant participants had higher prevalence of clinically significant fibrosis than insulin-sensitive participants (≥F2: 10% vs. <1%; p<0.001). They also had greater hepatic steatosis, higher ALT, AST, CK-18, HbA1c, and adipose tissue insulin resistance (Adipo-IR) levels, and lower adiponectin concentrations (all p<0.001). Fibrosis was infrequent among insulin-sensitive participants and almost exclusively limited to mild fibrosis (stage F1). Among participants with steatosis, ≥F2 fibrosis was present in 1% of insulin-sensitive participants compared with 13% of insulin-resistant participants (p<0.001). Conclusions Clinically significant fibrosis (≥F2) was uncommon among insulin-sensitive individuals with T2D and largely limited to mild fibrosis (F1). HOMA-IR <2.5 identified a subgroup at very low risk for fibrosis, supporting its potential use as a simple, clinically accessible tool for MASLD risk stratification in primary care and endocrinology settings.

title: Machine Learning Models Combining [<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET Radiomics and Clinical Features to Predict Overall Survival for Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer Treated with [<sup>177</sup>Lu]Lu-PSMA Radioligand Therapy.
abstract: Purpose Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remains incurable despite recent therapeutic advances. [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT (lutetium-177 labelled prostate-specific membrane antigen radioligand therapy) provides meaningful clinical benefit in selected patients. However, ∼30% of the patients do not respond to [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. Although several baseline prognostic factors are well known, reliable pretherapeutic predictive biomarkers are still lacking. We developed and compared several predictive machine learning (ML) models integrating clinical, biochemical, and imaging data, including [ 68 Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET (gallium-68 labelled prostate-specific membrane antigen ligand positron emission tomography) radiomic features, to estimate overall survival (OS) in patients with mCRPC treated with [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. Methods This retrospective monocentric study included 102 patients with mCRPC treated with [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA between January 2022 and March 2024. Five lesions per patient were segmented on their pretherapeutic [ 68 Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/computed tomography (CT) scans. Radiomic features were extracted following Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative guidelines. Multimodal ML models integrating clinical, genomic, biochemical, and imaging features (including radiomics) were developed to predict OS. Results Median OS of the total cohort was 11.2 mo. Intralesional homogeneity, characterized by the second-order radiomic feature normalized inverse difference moment, was associated with shorter OS (p = 0.025). The best-performing ML model achieved a 12-mo area under the curve (AUC) of 0.778 by combining 22 clinical, biochemical, genomic, and radiomic features. The model leveraging PET data alone achieved strong performance, with an AUC comparable to the clinical model (0.715 vs 0.766). Conclusions ML models based on [ 68 Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT, including radiomic features, offer a noninvasive, standardized, and widely accessible approach to predict OS in patients with mCRPC treated with [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. This study highlights the strong predictive potential of PSMA PET imaging for patient stratification in a real-world setting.

title: Clinical T staging accuracy and its prognostic relevance in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Accurate clinical T-staging is essential for guiding surgical management in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), particularly when determining treatment escalation or de-escalation. This study evaluated its diagnostic accuracy and impact on potential over- and undertreatment. This retrospective single-center study included patients with histologically confirmed OSCC who underwent primary surgical resection with negative margins between 2012 and 2022. Clinical T-staging based on preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography and clinical examination was compared with pathological staging. The primary endpoint was the diagnostic accuracy of clinical T-staging, while secondary endpoints were overall survival and disease-free survival. title: Optimizing Echocardiographic Evaluation of Chronic Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Implications for Guideline Recommendations.
abstract: Background The ASE (American Society of Echocardiography) guidelines recommend the presence of at least 4 specific criteria to confirm a diagnosis of definite severe mitral regurgitation (MR). However, the performance of these criteria, particularly when <4 are present, remains unclear. Objectives This study aims to evaluate and optimize the ASE native MR guidelines by comparing them with quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), considered the reference standard for MR assessment. Methods In this prospective study, 177 patients underwent near-simultaneous CMR and transthoracic echocardiography for the assessment of MR. MR severity was classified using a 4-grade scale based on CMR-derived regurgitant volume, which was calculated as the difference between total left ventricular (LV) stroke volume and aortic forward flow. MR severity was similarly graded using the ASE algorithm, with quantification performed when necessary, by averaging the regurgitant volume from 3 methods: 1) the proximal isovelocity surface area method; 2) the biplane LV volumetric method; and 3) the mitral valve volumetric method. Results The study cohort had a median age of 61.7 years, with 55% being men. Primary MR was the predominant pathology (73% of patients), with 42% having mitral valve prolapse and 25% presenting with flail leaflets. There was exact agreement between transthoracic echocardiography and CMR MR grading in 51% of cases, whereas agreement within 1 grade was observed in 89%. Patients who met any of the ASE severe MR criteria were predominantly classified as having grades 3 to 4 MR by CMR. The following ASE parameters demonstrated high specificity for identifying grade 4 MR by CMR: pulmonary vein systolic flow reversal (specificity 88%), enlarged LV with normal systolic function (specificity 85%), proximal isovelocity surface area radius ≥1.0 cm (specificity 83%), and vena contracta width ≥0.7 cm (specificity 80%). Combining color Doppler with either pulmonary vein systolic reversal or enlarged LV with normal function resulted in 91%-95% specificity for severe MR. Importantly, reliance on fewer ASE criteria reduced the need for quantification from 86% (4 criteria) to 73% (3 criteria) and 59% (2 criteria), thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency. Conclusions Certain ASE criteria, especially when used in combination, are highly specific for diagnosing severe MR, even when <4 criteria are present. This study suggests that in many cases, the reliance on extensive quantification may be reduced, streamlining the diagnostic process and improving clinical workflow.

title: Differentiation of common liver tumors using tumor-to-liver contrast on routine non-contrast T<sub>2</sub>-weighted magnetic resonance imaging.
abstract: Introduction Accurate classification of liver tumors requires contrast-enhanced MRI. However, contrast agents are contraindicated in patients with renal impairment or allergies. Concerns regarding the environmental impact of gadolinium-based agents have increased. Thus, classification using non-contrast MRI is desirable. This study evaluated whether tumor-to-liver contrast (TLC) derived from T 2 -weighted imaging (T 2 WI) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), along with apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), can differentiate common liver tumors: hepatocellular carcinomas (HCCs), metastases, and hemangiomas. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 119 patients with 122 liver tumors undergoing liver MRI. We calculated TLC from T 2 WI and DWI (b = 1000 s/mm²), and measured ADC values. Tumors were classified as HCCs, metastases, or hemangiomas based on radiological or pathological findings. Analyses were stratified by liver function using the albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score. Group differences were assessed using the Kruskal-Wallis and Steel-Dwass tests. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using one-versus-rest receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results T 2 WI-derived TLC differed significantly among tumor types (p < 0.05) and was highest in hemangiomas, followed by metastases and HCCs. DWI-derived TLC and ADC values differed in some tumor comparisons but showed greater variability and overlap. These patterns persisted after ALBI stratification. ROC analysis showed that T 2 WI-derived TLC performed well for hemangiomas (AUC = 0.975) and HCC (AUC = 0.839), whereas ADC performed best for metastases (AUC = 0.716). Overall, T 2 WI-derived TLC outperformed DWI-derived TLC. Conclusions TLC derived from non-contrast T 2 WI may serve as a practical, observer-independent marker for differentiating liver tumors, particularly in patients who cannot receive contrast agents. Plain language summary MRI scans with contrast agents are often used to identify different types of liver tumors, but some people cannot safely receive these agents. This study reviewed MRI scans from people with liver tumors and examined whether measurements from standard non-contrast MRI images could help distinguish between common tumor types. This study found that a measurement taken from T 2 -weighted MRI images was particularly effective at differentiating liver tumors, especially hemangiomas and hepatocellular carcinoma, without the need for contrast agents. This matters because non-contrast MRI methods may help support diagnosis in people who cannot receive contrast agents and may reduce reliance on these substances.

title: Accelerated 3D Late Gadolinium Enhancement Pulse Sequence with Isotropic Spatial Resolution, Self-Navigation of Respiratory Motion, and Arrhythmia Rejection for Quantification of Left Atrial Fibrosis in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
abstract: Background The left atrium (LA) is a thin structure (1.5-2.5mm). Conventional 3D late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) pulse sequences for imaging the LA typically have limited through-plane resolution (2.5-5mm) or prolonged scan times (10-15min), resulting in poor image quality and limited clinical translatability. We sought to develop and test whether a 3D LGE pulse sequence featuring 1.5mm³ isotropic spatial resolution and a predictable scan time of 600 heartbeats can produce diagnostically acceptable image quality at 1.5T for quantification of LA structural remodeling in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). Methods A 3D LGE pulse sequence was developed using gradient-recalled echo (GRE) readout, stack-of-stars k-space sampling with variable density along the partition direction, retrospective arrhythmia rejection, and XD-GRASP reconstruction with self-navigation of respiratory motion. Thirty patients with AF (twenty imaged prior to first-time ablation, ten prior to repeat ablation) and twenty healthy controls were scanned using this pulse sequence. The upper limit of normal image intensity ratio (IIR) was derived from the control group; specifically, 2 standard deviations (SDs) above the mean. Suspected LA fibrosis was quantified by one rater. Two cardiothoracic radiologists independently graded the image quality across three categories (conspicuity, artifacts, noise) using a 5-point Likert scale per category, with a score of 3 considered clinically acceptable. Results The proposed pulse sequence produced diagnostically acceptable image quality scores in all three categories for AF and control cohorts. Retrospective rejection of data acquired during ectopic heartbeats significantly (p<0.05) improved contrast-to-noise ratio (+3.7%) and sharpness (blur metric -3.2%) metrics, albeit at the expense of a significantly reduced signal-to-noise ratio (-4.4%). The upper limit of normal IIR was 1.43. Using this cutoff value to identify suspected LA fibrosis, compared with the control group (2.47 ± 2.24%), the first-time ablation group (7.45 ± 7.38%) was not significantly different (p = 0.14), whereas the repeat ablation group (14.94 ± 13.83%) was significantly different (p < 0.05). Conclusion The proposed pulse sequence produces diagnostically acceptable image quality at 1.5T and provides evidence of LA structural remodeling in AF patients, including greater suspected LA fibrosis burden, relative to control subjects.

title: VIRTUAL REALITY-ENHANCED FOR PREOPERATIVE ANATOMICAL ASSESSMENT OF ABDOMINAL NEUROBLASTOMA: A COMPARATIVE STUDY WITH CONVENTIONAL CT IMAGING.
abstract: Aim Accurate assessment of tumour anatomy is critical for neuroblastoma surgical planning. This study evaluated whether patient-specific virtual reality (VR) models improve the accuracy of pre-operative anatomical assessment compared with conventional computed tomography (CT) imaging. Methods CT scans from nine patients with abdominal neuroblastoma were segmented to create patient-specific VR models, which were then imported into an in-house VR application. Eleven paediatric surgeons (n=5 consultants; n=6 registrars) independently evaluated conventional CT images and VR reconstructions to assess vascular and organ involvement, image-defined risk factors (IDRFs), and operative strategies. Anatomical accuracy was quantified against intraoperative findings recorded in the International Neuroblastoma Surgical Report Form. Subjective ratings were collected using Likert scales. Mixed-effects models and non-parametric statistical analyses were conducted (p<0.05). Results VR significantly improved overall anatomical accuracy, with a mean increase of 12.4 percentage points (95% CI 8.5-16.3; p<0.0001). Improvements were observed for vascular involvement (+12.5%, p<0.001), organ involvement (+9.6%, p<0.01), and IDRF identification (+13.7%, p<0.0001). Improvements in anatomical accuracy with VR were similar between consultants and registrars. VR did not significantly alter operative planning decisions or predicted tumour resectability. Surgeons reported greater confidence in anatomical understanding and surgical planning with VR than CT (p<0.001). The VR platform received high ratings for usability, integration into the preoperative planning workflow, and perceived clinical value. Conclusion VR improved surgeons' anatomical assessment accuracy and confidence compared with traditional CT scans, highlighting VR's potential as a useful supplement to conventional imaging for preoperative evaluation in complex abdominal neuroblastoma.

title: Serum extracellular vesicle-associated SNORD54 adds diagnostic information to CEA and CYFRA21-1 in non-small cell lung cancer: a case-control development study.
abstract: Background Blood-based biomarkers that complement established serum markers may improve molecular classification of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We evaluated whether SNORD54 and SNORD41 measured in a serum extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and cytokeratin 19 fragment 21-1 (CYFRA21-1). Methods This single-center case-control biomarker-development study included serum samples from patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC and contemporaneous healthy controls. Supporting expression evidence was assessed in paired lung adenocarcinoma and lung squamous cell carcinoma datasets and in 48 paired formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded NSCLC specimens. Serum analyses included gene-specific cohorts and a common complete-case cohort with SNORD54, SNORD41, CEA, and CYFRA21-1 measurements. Logistic regression models were compared using paired DeLong tests. Model parsimony, adjustment for age, sex, and smoking, locked Stage I-II and Stage I subgroup analyses, U6-normalization sensitivity analyses, and 2,000-resample bootstrap internal validation were performed. Results The complete-case cohort comprised 98 patients with NSCLC and 79 healthy controls. Adding SNORD54 to CEA and CYFRA21-1 increased the AUC from 0.851(95% confidence interval [CI], 0.795-0.907) to 0.951 (95% CI, 0.920-0.982; ΔAUC, 0.100; 95% CI, 0.050-0.150; P<0.001). At the development-derived cutoff, the three-marker model achieved 85.7% sensitivity and 94.9% specificity. SNORD41 did not improve the SNORD54-containing model (ΔAUC, 0.0003; P=0.480; likelihood-ratio P=0.953) and increased both Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. With coefficients and the cutoff fixed from the overall cohort, the three-marker model achieved AUCs of 0.904 (95% CI, 0.843-0.964) for Stage I-II disease and 0.882 (95% CI, 0.804-0.960) for Stage I disease. SNORD54 remained informative after adjustment for age, sex, and smoking. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.948. U6 Ct values differed between diagnostic groups; associations of both snoRNAs with case status persisted in sensitivity models accounting for U6 Ct. Conclusions SNORD54 measured in a serum EV-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond CEA and CYFRA21-1 in this NSCLC case-control cohort. The parsimonious SNORD54 + CEA + CYFRA21-1 model retained discrimination in locked early-stage subgroup analyses and showed limited apparent optimism after bootstrap correction. Independent validation in cohorts that include benign pulmonary nodules and other relevant lung diseases, together with standardized EV processing and validated RNA normalization, will define the clinical transportability of this three-marker panel.

title: Characterizing age-dependent diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility properties in 5xFAD Alzheimer's mouse brain using high-resolution MRI.
abstract: Background and purpose Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating and progressive neurodegenerative disorder and the most common cause of dementia. This study aimed to characterize magnetic susceptibility changes associated with beta-amyloid (Aβ) plaques during AD progression using diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility measurements in the 5xFAD mouse model. Methods Ex vivo multi-echo gradient-echo imaging (MGRE) with a spatial resolution of 40 × 40 × 40 μm 3 was performed in three age groups of 5xFAD mice (4, 12, and 18 months) using a 9.4T Bruker MRI scanner. Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) was reconstructed, and DECOMPOSE-QSM was applied to derive diamagnetic component susceptibility (DCS) and paramagnetic component susceptibility (PCS). Aβ plaques were automatically detected based on DCS and quantified to assess age-dependent plaque accumulation, changes in plaque burden, and associated susceptibility alterations. Cortical regions were further segmented into plaque-detected and plaque-undetected regions to assess regional susceptibility variations among the three age groups. In addition, Aβ/ferritin immunostaining was performed on the imaged murine brains. Results The results demonstrated progressive, spatially heterogeneous, age-dependent accumulation of amyloid plaques, as evidenced by significant increases in plaque burden. In plaque-detected and whole-region cortical areas, DCS consistently shifted toward more negative values (greater diamagnetic susceptibility) with disease progression, while PCS became more positive (greater paramagnetic susceptibility). The concurrent increase in plaque burden, together with progressively more negative DCS and more positive PCS within plaques, is consistent with increasing diamagnetic and paramagnetic tissue contributions associated with amyloid and iron-related pathology, respectively. Histological analysis showed colocalized Aβ aggregation and ferritin deposition within plaques, both of which increased with age. Conclusions The decomposed susceptibility components, DCS and PCS, provide complementary biophysical information beyond conventional QSM, enabling improved characterization of plaque-associated susceptibility changes during AD progression. High-resolution MRI facilitates the visualization and detection of individual plaques, allowing detailed analysis of their susceptibility properties. These findings highlight the importance of high-resolution MRI and the potential of diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility measures as sensitive imaging biomarkers for monitoring neurodegenerative pathology.

title: Achieving detailed medial temporal lobe segmentation with upsampled isotropic training from implicit neural representation.
abstract: Imaging biomarkers in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are important tools for diagnosing, tracking and treating Alzheimer's disease (AD). Neurofibrillary tau pathology in AD is closely linked to neurodegeneration and generally follows a pattern of spread in the brain, with early stages involving subregions of the medial temporal lobe (MTL). Accurate segmentation of MTL subregions is needed to extract granular biomarkers of AD progression. MTL subregions are often imaged using T2-weighted (T2w) MRI scans that are highly anisotropic due to constraints of MRI physics and image acquisition, making it difficult to reliably model MTL subregions geometrically and extract morphological measures, such as thickness. In this study, we propose a segmentation framework for MTL subregions in isotropic space, in which an implicit neural representation is used to construct the isotropic training atlas from the anisotropic low-resolution T2w data, with T1w MRI as an auxiliary modality to support the INR and segmentation. In an independent test set, the morphological measures extracted using this isotropic model showed stronger effect sizes than those from models trained on anisotropic data in distinguishing participants with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from cognitively unimpaired individuals. In the test-retest analysis, the morphological measures extracted using the isotropic model showed greater stability than those from the anisotropic segmentation. This study demonstrates improved reliability of MRI-derived MTL subregion biomarkers without additional atlas annotation effort, which may more accurately quantify and track the relationship between AD pathology and brain atrophy for monitoring disease progression.

title: Behavioural and environmental strategies implemented by radiographers to care for patients with neurocognitive disorders during medical imaging and therapeutic procedures.
abstract: Introduction As the population ages, radiographers are increasingly likely to care for patients with dementia, Alzheimer's disease and other neurocognitive disorders in medical imaging or radiation therapy departments. Since the cognitive and behavioural presentation of these patients can vary, radiographers must be prepared to adapt their approach. To investigate behavioural and environmental strategies used by radiographers when caring for patients with neurocognitive disorders (NCDs) during medical imaging and radiation therapy procedures. Methods A cross-sectional survey comprising 18 questions was conducted among radiographers working across medical imaging and radiotherapy modalities. The questionnaire explored attitudes towards patients with NCDs, behavioural communication strategies, environmental adaptations, and institutional support measures. Descriptive statistics and thematic analysis of open-ended responses were performed. Results A total of 160 radiographers participated. Most respondents reported positive attitudes toward patients with NCDs, with 94% indicating no fear when interacting with this population. Behavioural communication strategies were frequently used, particularly maintaining eye contact (85%), using simple language (80%), and speaking slowly and clearly (76%). Caregivers were commonly involved to facilitate communication (81%). Despite this, 45% of radiographers reported frustration at not always knowing how to help effectively. Institutional environmental adaptations were limited, with most participants reporting no dementia-specific training (85%) or departmental protocols (78%). Conclusion Radiographers frequently implement behavioural strategies to support patients with NCDs, but this relies on individual initiative rather than structured organisational support, which remains limited. Implications for practice Radiographers should use clear, simple communication strategies with NCD patients, involve caregivers during imaging procedures, and develop dementia-specific training and departmental protocols.

title: MRI-Only Preoperative Localization and Semiautomated Three-Dimensional Modeling of the Cervical Vagus Nerve for Vagus Nerve Stimulation Implantation.
abstract: Background We evaluated whether three-dimensional steady-state free precession with time-spatial labeling inversion pulse (3D-SSFP with time-SLIP) MRI could localize the cervical vagus nerve before vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) implantation and developed training-data-free semiautomated vagus nerve tracking software. Methods Thirty patients with drug-resistant epilepsy underwent preoperative cervical 3D-SSFP with time-SLIP MRI followed by VNS implantation. The left vagus nerve was visually identified at the planned surgical level, and its relationship to the common carotid artery (CCA) and internal jugular vein (IJV) was classified. MRI localization was validated against intraoperative findings. A MATLAB-based tool semi-automatically tracked the vagus nerve, CCA, and IJV from user-defined reference points. Accuracy was assessed using coordinate error and classification agreement. Results The vagus nerve was identified on MRI in all 30 patients, with complete concordance between MRI and intraoperative localization. Among 29 classifiable patients, the nerve was located superficially between the CCA and IJV in 45%, superficially and lateral to the CCA in 41%, deep between the CCA and IJV in 10%, and deep and medial to the CCA in 3.4%. The median distance between software-derived and visually identified coordinates was 1 mm (interquartile range, 1-2 mm), and software-derived classification agreed with consensus visual classification in 27 of 29 patients (93%). Conclusions Cervical MRI enabled preoperative localization of the vagus nerve and adjacent vessels. The semiautomated method showed close agreement with expert visual assessment and may support anatomical orientation and surgical planning for VNS implantation.

Cervical MRI enabled preoperative localization of the vagus nerve and adjacent vessels. The semiautomated method showed close agreement with expert visual assessment and may support anatomical orientation and surgical planning for VNS implantation.

title: Retrieval-induced forgetting and facilitation across the Alzheimer's disease continuum: Behavioral and neuroanatomical evidence from a recognition-based paradigm.
abstract: Objective The aim of the present study was to investigate facilitation (FAC) and retrieval-induced forgetting (RIF) during episodic memory retrieval across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum and to examine their gray matter correlates in verbal and visual recognition tasks. Method One hundred participants (28 AD, 29 amnestic mild cognitive impairment, 23 subjective cognitive decline [SCD], 20 healthy subjects) completed a modified retrieval-practice paradigm (mRPP) involving verbal and visual recognition tasks, a comprehensive neuropsychological battery, and 3T magnetic resonance imaging. FAC and RIF were computed at the group level and via individual proxy scores, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess the association between mRPP indices and regional gray matter volumes. Results The verbal mRPP showed reduced overall recognition in AD compared with healthy subjects ( p = .003 - η p ² = 0.23). A robust FAC effect in AD, amnestic mild cognitive impairment, and SCD was observed, whereas RIF emerged only in SCD, suggesting intact inhibitory control at the earliest stage and its disruption with disease progression ( p < .001 - η p ² = 0.48). The visual mRPP showed a strong FAC effect across all groups, with no RIF, indicating modality-specific reliance on recognition-based retrieval ( p < .001 - η p ² = 0.63). Voxel-based morphometry analyses revealed distinct gray matter correlates across groups and tasks: Verbal RIF was negatively associated with frontotemporal regions in AD patients and parieto-occipital regions in healthy subjects, while visual indices showed widespread associations with temporal, subcortical, cerebellar, and sensorimotor regions, particularly in amnestic mild cognitive impairment and SCD groups. Conclusions This study shows shared and modality-specific brain mechanisms of retrieval practice across AD stages. Preserved compensatory processes in SCD individuals give way to progressive regional disruption, supporting early, modality-tailored, and multimodal cognitive interventions to enhance cognition and delay cognitive decline. title: Cardiometabolic health's influence on the efficacy of pre-operative hormone therapy for men with localized high-risk prostate cancer.
abstract: Background Altered lipid metabolism, adiposity, and androgens have been linked to cardiac disease and prostate cancer. Adiposity increases risk of recurrence for prostate cancer and may enhance response to androgen receptor pathway inhibition (ARPI). We evaluated whether adiposity and circulating lipid metabolites are associated with response to pre-operative ADT + /- ARPI in localized high-risk prostate cancer (HRPCa). Methods We performed a post hoc analysis of 104 men with localized HRPCa treated with 3-6 months of preoperative ADT + /- ARPI across three trials. Body composition was quantified from L3 CT imaging at baseline and at radical prostatectomy (RP; end-of-treatment [EOT] n = 56). Plasma lipid metabolites were profiled by UPLC-MS at baseline (n = 60) and in paired baseline/EOT samples (n = 59). Pathologic response was defined as ≤ T2N0 at RP. PSA progression-free survival (PFS) was defined as time from RP to PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL or initiation of radiotherapy. Results Median age was 63 years, 76.9% had Gleason grade group 4-5, and 43.7% had clinical T3-4 disease. At RP, lower visceral (VATi, p = 0.002) and subcutaneous adiposity (SATi, p = 0.004) were associated with pathologic response. Increasing adiposity at RP was associated with PSA progression (per 10-unit increase: VATi HR 1.09, p = 0.04; SATi HR 1.14, p = 0.03). In paired analyses (n = 59), pathologic responders demonstrated decreases (p < 0.05) in diacylglycerols and polyunsaturated fatty acyl chain-containing triacylglycerols (PUFA-TAGs) and elevations in ceramide species. Non-responders exhibited increases (p < 0.05) in PUFA-TAGs and glycerophospholipids with reductions in lysophosphatidylcholine species, long-chain acylcarnitine, and cholesterol. Conclusions Higher post-treatment adiposity and intrapatient changes in lipid metabolite pathways were associated with inferior outcomes after pre-operative hormone therapy, supporting a stage-dependent link between cardiometabolic health and prostate cancer that warrants further elucidation.

title: Current classification systems in slipped capital femoral epiphysis: Clinical relevance, limitations, and future directions.
abstract: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) is the most common adolescent hip disorder and remains a significant cause of pain, gait disturbance, proximal femoral deformity, and early degenerative hip disease. Accurate classification of SCFE is essential for diagnosis, prognostication, treatment planning, and communication among orthopedic surgeons. Over the past several decades, multiple classification systems have been proposed based on symptom duration, physeal stability, radiographic severity, and deformity morphology. However, substantial variability exists regarding their reliability, prognostic value, and clinical applicability. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the currently available classification systems in SCFE, including temporal, Loder, Southwick, Wilson, epiphyseal tubercle (Maranho), MRI-based, and three-dimensional/statistical shape modeling classifications. Particular emphasis is placed on their historical evolution, clinical relevance, prognostic implications, limitations, and emerging role in modern hip preservation strategies. Among existing systems, the Loder classification remains the most clinically influential because of its strong association with avascular necrosis risk, while the Southwick classification continues to play a central role in quantifying deformity severity and guiding surgical decision-making. Emerging imaging-based and three-dimensional classifications have improved understanding of the rotational and multiplanar nature of SCFE and may facilitate earlier diagnosis, improved deformity characterization, and individualized treatment planning. Nevertheless, no single classification system comprehensively integrates physeal stability, deformity severity, vascular compromise, cartilage injury, and long-term functional prognosis. Current SCFE classification systems remain valuable tools in contemporary clinical practice; however, important limitations persist regarding reproducibility, prognostic accuracy, and integration with modern biomechanical concepts. Future classification frameworks may benefit from a multidomain approach integrating physeal stability, deformity morphology, vascular and biological status, cartilage involvement, and patient-specific prognostic factors, with prospective multicentre validation required before clinical adoption.

title: Acute Enlargement of a Frontal Calvarial Lesion in Polyostotic Fibrous Dysplasia Associated with McCune-Albright Syndrome: A Case Report.
abstract: Background McCune-Albright syndrome is a rare mosaic disorder caused by postzygotic activating mutations in GNAS , classically presenting with fibrous dysplasia (FD), hyperpigmented macules, and endocrinopathies. Craniofacial FD is common and typically follows a benign course. However, acute symptomatic changes with aggressive imaging features may mimic malignant transformation or secondary lesions such as aneurysmal bone cysts (ABCs), creating significant diagnostic uncertainty. Case Description We report a 20-year-old woman with known MAS and polyostotic FD who presented with a 4-week history of progressive left frontal swelling, headache, and tenderness. Interval imaging revealed a rapidly enlarging erosive lytic lesion of the left frontal calvarium with peripheral enhancement and an internal fluid-fluid level, raising concern for secondary pathology or malignancy. Given rapid growth and cortical erosion, the patient underwent surgical resection with cranioplasty. Intraoperatively, the lesion contained serosanguinous fluid. Histopathology demonstrated bland spindle cell proliferation with curvilinear woven bone trabeculae and hemosiderin-laden macrophages, without cytologic atypia, necrosis, or features of ABC. Molecular testing confirmed a GNAS p.(R201C) mutation, consistent with FD. The patient had an uncomplicated postoperative course with complete symptom resolution. Conclusion This case highlights that fluid-fluid levels, rapid interval growth, and erosive changes can occur in craniofacial FD without ABC formation or malignant transformation. Imaging findings alone are insufficient to distinguish benign changes from aggressive pathology. Accurate diagnosis requires a multimodal approach integrating clinical context, advanced imaging, histopathology, and pathologic analysis. Surgical intervention is justified in some cases to establish diagnosis and provide symptomatic relief.

title: Tenosynovitis caused by Mycobacterium malmoense.
abstract: Background Mycobacterium malmoense is a slow-growing nontuberculous mycobacterium (NTM) increasingly recognized as a cause of extrapulmonary infections. Tenosynovitis due to M. malmoense is rare and diagnostically challenging because of its indolent course and nonspecific clinical presentation. Case presentation We report a 65-year-old immunocompetent woman presenting with progressive wrist pain, swelling, and impaired hand function without prior trauma. Symptoms developed after exposure to fresh fish and shellfish. Surgical exploration revealed extensive tenosynovitis with median nerve compression. Histopathology showed granulomatous synovitis suggestive of mycobacterial infection. Molecular testing detected Mycobacterium genus DNA, while PCR for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex was negative. After prolonged incubation, culture identified M. malmoense . Drug susceptibility testing demonstrated susceptibility to standard antimycobacterial agents except doxycycline. Initial empiric therapy targeting M. marinum was adapted following species identification. After 8 months of treatment, significant clinical and radiological improvement was observed, with no evidence of relapse at 6-month follow-up. Discussion M. malmoense tenosynovitis is extremely rare, with only few cases reported. Diagnosis is frequently delayed due to low sensitivity of microscopy, slow growth in culture, and nonspecific findings. Molecular diagnostics and prolonged incubation are essential. Management requires a combination of surgery and prolonged antimycobacterial therapy. Conclusion NTM infections, including M. malmoense , should be considered in chronic tenosynovitis unresponsive to standard treatment. Early diagnostic suspicion and interdisciplinary management are crucial for favorable outcomes.

title: Multimodal based Brain Tumor Classification using Clustered Federated Learning in Edge based IoT Network.
abstract: A brain tumor is characterized by the uncontrolled growth of cells that causes a severe impact on the quality of life. Nowadays, various methods based on multimodal medical images are used to identify brain tumors. Meanwhile, these methods require extensive amounts of labeled information to identify disease tissues and often encounter various challenges based on privacy and accuracy. This paper establishes a Taylor-based Focal Log-cosh Entropy Network (TFLE-Net) to classify brain tumors from demographic data and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images by utilizing clustered federated learning in an edge-based Internet of Things (IoT) network. The detection process is executed in clustered federated learning concerning two entities: server and nodes. In a local training model, an input MRI scan is pre-processed, further brain tumor areas are segmented, and then, the mining of various features is performed. Simultaneously, the normalization of input demographic data is done, and the suitable features are selected using information gain. Further, the extracted features and chosen features are subjected to TFLE-Net to classify brain tumors. Additionally, the TFLE-Net yielded Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.057, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.047, True Positive Rate (TPR) of 97.789%, and accuracy of 96.987%.

title: Posterior Scleritis Following Uneventful Small-Incision Cataract Surgery.
abstract: Background Posterior scleritis following routine, uncomplicated cataract surgery in a patient without underlying systemic disease is an exceedingly rare and potentially sight-threatening clinical entity. Method A 55-year-old female with no systemic medical history presented three weeks after uneventful small-incision cataract surgery (SICS) in the right eye with sudden vision loss, redness, and severe ocular pain exacerbated by eye movements. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) had deteriorated from 6/9 to finger counting close to her face. Dilated fundus examination revealed multiple dull yellow subretinal lesions across the posterior pole. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed hyperreflective vitreous cells, subretinal fluid (SRF), and choroidal undulations. B-scan ultrasonography confirmed diffuse posterior scleritis, demonstrating localized sclerochoroidal thickening and fluid accumulation in the sub-Tenon's space. Comprehensive laboratory testing and imaging ruled out infectious and autoimmune etiologies. Result The patient was treated with high-dose intravenous pulse methylprednisolone (1 g/day for three days) followed by an oral prednisolone taper, which led to immediate pain relief and anatomical resolution. At six months, the scleritis had completely resolved with a BCVA improvement to 6/12, limited by persistent localized disruption of the foveal ellipsoid zone on OCT. The patient remained recurrence-free at six months. Conclusion Diffuse posterior scleritis can occur as a postoperative inflammatory phenomenon following uneventful cataract surgery. Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion, utilize B-scan ultrasonography for diagnosis, and initiate prompt systemic corticosteroid therapy to optimize anatomical and visual outcomes.

title: Bone microarchitecture, density, and strength assessment in automotive trauma patients using HR-pQCT: a pilot study.
abstract: Objective Automotive trauma patients enrolled in the Crash Injury Research and Engineering Network (CIREN) typically undergo computed tomography (CT) imaging as part of emergency care. HR-pQCT is a noninvasive imaging technique that enables assessment of bone microarchitecture at the peripheral sites. CT and HR-pQCT can be used to estimate volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) and strength via finite element analysis (FEA). However, HR-pQCT's superior resolution (approximately 10 times higher than conventional clinical CT scanners) captures in vivo trabecular and cortical microarchitecture, enabling high fidelity FEA. This study examines HR-pQCT-derived bone microarchitecture and strength measurements in relation to fracture patterns, bone-related comorbidities, and CT-derived vBMD in CIREN trauma patients, while providing foundational evidence to support HR-pQCT use following motor vehicle crashes (MVC) and pedestrian crashes. Methods Nine automotive trauma patients (ages 17-76; 78% female) enrolled at Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center from the National Highway Safety Administration's CIREN study participated in the HR-pQCT pilot study. HR-pQCT scans were acquired within 1-12 months following the patient's MVC ( n = 7) or pedestrian crash ( n = 2). Scans were acquired at four sites: 1) distal tibia, 2) diaphyseal tibia, 3) distal radius, and 4) diaphyseal radius. HR-pQCT normative percentiles were determined using Indiana University's calculator. Descriptive statistics were used to present HR-pQCT musculoskeletal outcomes based on bone-related comorbidities, BMI, and fracture incidence. Pearson correlations were performed between HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia and radius total vBMD and CT-derived total vBMD at the spine and femoral compartments. Results At the distal tibia, participants without tibia and fibula fractures tended to show greater mean cortical thickness (1.63 ± 0.38 versus 1.15 ± 0.05 mm), cortical area (146.24 ± 46.07 versus 103.70 ± 1.70 mm 2 ), cortical vBMD (943.83 ± 79.18 versus 861.05 ± 26.52 mg HA/cm 3 ), and bone strength (10.25 ± 3.72 versus 7.00 ± 0.70 kN). Additionally, HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia total vBMD demonstrated a strong positive correlation with CT-derived femoral head total vBMD ( r = 0.766; p = 0.045). Normative percentiles showed that participants with bone-related comorbidities had lower bone microarchitectural and strength percentiles than the group without comorbidities. Conclusion This study demonstrates the viability of HR-pQCT for characterizing bone microarchitecture, strength, and density in automotive trauma patients and identifying differences that might relate to fracture and bone-related comorbidities. These preliminary findings support incorporating HR-pQCT imaging into automotive crash research due to its ability to provide detailed cortical and trabecular microarchitectural measurements that are not available from clinical CT.

title: Spinal neurocysticercosis: synthesizing evidence on clinical presentations, anatomical patterns, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Spinal neurocysticercosis (NCC) is an uncommon manifestation of NCC involving the spinal cord, meninges, nerve roots, and subarachnoid spaces. Although less common than intracranial disease, spinal involvement can cause substantial neurological morbidity because even small lesions within the confined spinal canal may produce progressive myelopathy. Disease may result from hematogenous dissemination or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) spread of Taenia solium larvae and may present as intramedullary, intradural extramedullary, subarachnoid, or, rarely, extradural lesions. Clinical manifestations are diverse and include paraparesis, quadriparesis, cauda equina syndrome, and chronic meningitis. Magnetic resonance imaging is the diagnostic modality of choice, providing detailed assessment of lesion location, evolutionary stage, inflammatory activity, and associated complications. CSF analysis and immunological or molecular tests provide supportive evidence, while histopathological examination confirms the diagnosis when tissue is available. Treatment is individualized and may include antiparasitic agents, corticosteroids, and surgery when indicated. Although outcomes are generally favorable with early diagnosis and appropriate treatment, delayed treatment, extensive arachnoiditis, diffuse leptomeningeal disease, and established spinal cord damage may result in permanent neurological deficits. Further prospective studies are needed to refine diagnostic strategies and optimize management. PubMed database was searched from inception to 13 July 2026, for spinal neurocysticercosis and spinal cysticercosis.

title: GPT-assisted radiomic modeling for predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Objective . To evaluate whether GPT can assist in automating radiomics modeling for predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Methods. The study included a training cohort (TC; n = 186), a validation cohort (VC; n = 116), and a prospective multicenter validation cohort (PVC; n = 269). Radiomic and supervised deep learning features were extracted from pretreatment T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging. logistic regression (LR) was first evaluated using radiomic, deep learning, and fused features. Support vector machine, naïve Bayes, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting models were subsequently compared using fused features. GPT was not used as the classifier but assisted with preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter optimization, code generation and execution, model training, and probability output. Each GPT-assisted workflow was independently repeated five times. Results. Fused features achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for both manually developed and GPT-assisted LR models. Their AUCs were 0.759 versus 0.763 ± 0.003 in the TC, 0.714 versus 0.741 ± 0.008 in the VC, and 0.700 versus 0.706 ± 0.004 in the PVC. Across five classifiers, GPT-assisted workflows achieved performance broadly comparable to manually developed models. Repeated GPT-assisted runs showed limited variability, with AUC standard deviations ranging from 0.001 to 0.019. Conclusion. Under expert supervision, GPT can automate key radiomics modeling procedures while achieving performance comparable to conventional machine learning workflows, potentially reducing technical workload and facilitating integrated model development.

title: Multi-GPU parallel framework for DOI-enabled long axial field-of-view PET image reconstruction.
abstract: Objective. Depth-of-interaction (DOI)-enabled long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) positron emission tomography (PET) can mitigate parallax-induced resolution degradation, but DOI modeling substantially expands the lines-of-response space and increases computational cost. This study aimed to develop a scalable reconstruction framework for DOI-enabled LAFOV-PET. Approach. We present an optimized multi-GPU reconstruction framework based on list-mode ordered-subsets expectation maximization. The framework targets the major computational bottlenecks of DOI-enabled LAFOV-PET reconstruction, including sensitivity image calculation and Monte Carlo-based scatter estimation. Main results. The extended IQ phantom demonstrated near-linear scalability across multiple GPUs for sensitivity image calculation and Monte Carlo-based scatter estimation. Additional Derenzo and hybrid anthropomorphic phantom studies validated the imaging benefits of DOI modeling, including improved spatial resolution and performance under realistic imaging conditions. Significance. The proposed framework improves the scalability of DOI-enabled LAFOV-PET reconstruction by enabling its dominant computational components to efficiently utilize available GPU resources, establishing a foundation for high-performance reconstruction in next-generation PET systems.
